Gifts and succession illustrate why technical transfer and tax recognition are not synonymous. Section 75 can describe an ownership event, while section 79 can require no gain or loss and preserve character and cost in qualifying transfers, including transmission on death and specified gifts. A 2026 cost rule for inherited immovable property does not supply a corresponding virtual-asset fair-value step-up. Executors therefore need the deceased’s original acquisition, wallet and control records; a market quotation at death cannot by itself replace the statutory cost rule.244

The matrix is not a schedule of new taxes. It is a discipline for applying existing law and exposing the places where Parliament, FBR or a Provincial Legislature must speak more clearly.

11.3 Residence, Source and Cross-Border Activity

Distributed infrastructure does not abolish tax residence or geographical source. The Ordinance determines residence separately for individuals, companies and associations of persons. It then brings into a resident person’s total income the Pakistan-source and foreign-source amounts within the statutory framework, while a non-resident is generally within the charge for Pakistan-source income. Treaty relief, foreign-tax credit, exemptions and special regimes may modify the result; they do not permit residence to be inferred from an IP address or exchange location.245

For a resident business, section 101 treats business income as Pakistan-source to the extent derived from business carried on in Pakistan. For a non-resident, attribution may arise through a permanent establishment, sales through such establishment, a business connection or other specified connections. Gains on assets used in a relevant business, services, royalties, profit on debt and other categories have their own source rules. A virtual-asset analysis should therefore begin with the person and the income-producing activity: where management occurs; who contracts; where personnel and systems perform the service; whether an agent or permanent establishment acts; where rights and obligations are situated; and to what Pakistan activity income is attributable.

Section 101’s 2024 “significant economic presence” provisions extend the business-connection enquiry to prescribed levels of transactions in goods, services or property, including downloads of data or software, and to systematic and continuous interaction through digital means with a prescribed number of users in Pakistan. The text is relevant to foreign exchanges and platforms, but it is not a licence to tax global income by counting Pakistani app visits. The monetary or user threshold must be prescribed and met, a business connection must arise under the section, and only income attributable to the Pakistan connection is brought within the source rule.246

Certain attractive proxies are legally weak. The location of validating nodes does not necessarily identify the seller, service provider or owner. The situs of a private key says little where a cloud custodian, multisignature group or recovery provider participates. A domain name, downloadable app or Pakistani customer may support an evidential nexus, but none replaces the statutory source test. Conversely, a foreign-incorporated platform with management, personnel, agents or sustained service operations in Pakistan cannot defeat the source enquiry merely by settling transactions on a borderless ledger.

The minimum cross-border file should record:

  • taxpayer residence and the legal basis for it;
  • counterparty and beneficial-owner identity where required and obtainable;
  • contracting entity, customer terms and place of management;
  • service-performance and personnel locations;
  • permanent-establishment, agent and significant-economic-presence facts;
  • wallet, custodian and platform roles without treating them as conclusive situs;
  • gross receipts, attributable functions, assets, risks and expenses;
  • foreign tax paid and treaty relied upon; and
  • the method used to allocate a multi-jurisdictional transaction.

Withholding must be tested separately. A payment to a non-resident may fall within section 152 or another provision only if the statutory payment, payer, recipient and source conditions are satisfied. Converting the payment into a token does not avoid an otherwise applicable duty; it also does not create a withholding duty absent those elements. The proposed corrective regime should specify how an in-kind payer determines the amount, funds the withholding, reports the asset transfer and handles a transaction where no fiat is available, without imposing confiscatory over-withholding on gross transaction value.

11.4 Valuation, Basis, Timing and Records

Volatility is not the legal reason valuation is difficult. The deeper problem is that “price” can refer to an order-book quote, executed trade, index, oracle, thin-liquidity pool, related-party transfer, locked token, redeemable claim or manipulated market. Section 68 uses an open-market fair-market-value standard and permits the Commissioner to determine value where it is not ordinarily ascertainable. Sections 69, 76 and 77 connect receipt, cost and consideration to the tax computation. These rules provide a foundation, but not a complete virtual-asset valuation protocol.247

A defensible methodology should apply a hierarchy:

1. use the actual arm’s-length transaction price on a reliable venue where it represents the rights transferred;

2. where that price is unavailable or distorted, use a documented volume-weighted or time-consistent composite from independent liquid venues;

3. value a redeemable claim by reference to enforceable redemption rights only after testing issuer credit, reserve access, fees, delay and restrictions;

4. for illiquid, vested, locked or rights-bearing tokens, apply an appropriate valuation technique and disclose restrictions, assumptions and uncertainty; and

5. where no reliable value can be established, preserve the evidence, state the uncertainty and use the statutory determination route rather than inventing precision.

The policy must fix a consistent valuation time and time zone. A daily closing price is administratively simple but can be arbitrary for intraday exchanges. Exact transaction-time valuation is more accurate but costly for high-frequency activity. A proportionate rule can require actual executed value where available, allow a prescribed daily method for qualifying retail volumes, and require transaction-time or independently substantiated valuation for related-party, illiquid or material transactions. The selected source, timestamp, asset pair, exchange rate, units, fees and fallback must be reproducible.

Section 71 converts foreign currency and Rupees at the State Bank rate on the relevant date; it does not classify every crypto-asset as foreign currency. A sound rule would establish fair value in reliable fiat and then translate it into Rupees at the lawful State Bank rate.

Basis must follow units through their life. Each taxpayer should maintain, at minimum: acquisition date and time; quantity and asset identifier; chain and contract address where relevant; legal rights; wallet or account; counterparty or venue; consideration and incidental fees; valuation source; transaction identifier; beneficial owner; tax character; transfer history; and disposal proceeds. Where units are pooled, the law or rules should choose a basis convention—such as specific identification supported by immutable records or a prescribed average—and prevent a taxpayer from changing methods opportunistically after prices move. Wrapped assets, bridges, migrations and redenominations require continuity records; they should not be assumed to be taxable or non-taxable merely from a new contract address.

Receipt under section 69 includes amounts actually received, applied on behalf of a person or made available. Rewards subject to a lock, slashing, unbonding period, governance condition or unresolved protocol claim require a facts-based control analysis. Recognition before the taxpayer can transfer or realise any enforceable benefit can tax an amount that never becomes available; indefinite deferral after control is obtained can conceal income. The record should identify the precise legal and technical event that made the reward available.

The Ordinance generally requires taxpayer records for six years after the relevant tax year, with longer retention where proceedings remain pending. Companies have separate books-and-records duties and a ten-year retention period. VASPs should adopt the longer applicable period and preserve the raw transaction ledger, customer subledger, pricing inputs and method versions—not only a year-end statement.248 Records must reconcile legal ownership, customer account, beneficial owner and technical movement so that neither self-transfers nor internal platform transfers are misclassified.

11.5 Treatment by Actor and Function

Tax classification should follow the actor’s function and the rights created. A single organisation may perform several functions, and each stream may have a different base.

Individuals and investors. Frequency, organisation, intention, financing, holding period, use of specialised systems and relation to an existing business can inform whether activity is a business or investment, but no single factor should be treated as conclusive. A holder must separately identify acquisitions, disposals, income rewards and personal-use assertions. Wealth-statement and foreign-asset obligations can exist even where no disposal gain arises.

VASPs. An exchange may earn trading commissions, spreads, listing fees, custody fees, withdrawal fees, staking commissions, data revenue and gains or losses on proprietary inventory. Customer gross trading volume is not the VASP’s income. Customer assets held without beneficial title should not be booked or taxed as the custodian’s own property merely because the custodian controls private keys. Proprietary positions and customer safeguarding balances require separate ledgers.

Brokers, dealers and market makers. A person trading as principal may hold stock-in-trade and recognise business profits; an agent ordinarily recognises commission rather than the customer’s gross consideration. A platform acting as both principal and agent must disclose the capacity in each transaction and prevent internal pricing from shifting profit between related entities or jurisdictions.

Issuers. Token issuance is not one tax event. A sale can represent an immediate supply, advance consideration for future performance, a borrowing or redeemable liability, a membership or governance right, an equity-like interest, a bundled arrangement or a transfer of property. Income recognition, deductions and sales-tax treatment follow the enforceable rights and performance obligations. Treasury tokens minted but not transferred do not automatically produce revenue; proceeds received for promised services do not automatically become tax-free capital.

Miners and validators. Commercial block-production or validation rewards may be business income, with ordinary-law treatment of allowable expenses. The legal recipient must be distinguished from pool operator, delegator and infrastructure host. Validator commission and delegator reward can have different character; later disposal is a separate event using the recognition value as basis.

Staking, lending and decentralised-finance arrangements. Labels such as “yield”, “interest”, “liquidity mining” or “staking” do not determine character. The enquiry asks whether the taxpayer transferred title, lent property, supplied a service, entered a partnership-like arrangement, received compensation for risk, disposed of one right for another, or merely delegated validation power. Protocol governance and smart-contract execution provide evidence of terms but do not replace the legal relationship.

Custodians and fiduciaries. The tax and accounting result turns on customer title, segregation, reuse rights, insolvency treatment, restitution obligation and beneficial entitlement. If terms permit the custodian to use assets and return an equivalent, the arrangement may be economically and legally closer to a loan than a bailment or safeguarding service. If title remains with the customer, platform control should not transform customer property into platform revenue.

Companies, funds, trusts and estates. Entity form, tax status and governing instrument matter. A company does not receive individual personal-use treatment. A fund or trust requires identification of the taxable person, beneficiaries and distributions. On death, the legal representative must secure wallet access and preserve basis; inheritance and later disposal are separate. The VAA creates no estate or succession tax charge.249

Actor-based rules should remain technology neutral but not evidence blind. They should require the information peculiar to virtual assets—wallets, contract rights, keys, transaction identifiers, chain events and venue pricing—only because those facts help apply the legal categories.

11.6 Withholding, Reporting and Tax Administration

A reporting system should make correct liability easier to determine; it should not substitute mass data for legal design. The existing Ordinance contains return, wealth-statement, foreign-income and foreign-asset, withholding-statement, information, record, audit and confidentiality machinery. It does not contain a complete virtual-asset reporting code.250

There is no general authority in the material inspected for a VASP to withhold tax from every virtual-asset disposal. Existing withholding sections can apply where their own conditions are met—for example, a relevant payment for goods or services or a payment to a non-resident—but a regulator should not direct a platform to deduct from gross customer proceeds without a clear charging and collection provision. Gross withholding is especially hazardous where only net profit is taxable, basis is held on another platform, the transfer is between the same owner’s wallets, or the customer has a loss.

Sections 165B and 165C must not be collapsed. Section 165B authorises specified information arrangements by financial institutions for automatic exchange under bilateral or multilateral instruments, with reportable-person and financial-institution terms taken from the Income Tax Rules. Section 165C requires quarterly information from online marketplaces, payment intermediaries and couriers in relation to digitally ordered goods and services. A VASP is not automatically within a full CARF regime merely because it is a digital platform, and a token transfer is not automatically a digitally ordered good or service.251

The domestic reporting layer should be enacted around a minimum, purpose-bound record:

  • taxpayer and controlling-person identity, residence and tax identification number;
  • licensed entity, service and account identifiers;
  • asset identifier, units and legal category used for tax treatment;
  • acquisition, disposal, transfer and reward event type;
  • fiat proceeds or fair market value, currency, valuation time and method;
  • fees, withholding where lawfully required and cost information actually held;
  • counterparty or destination category where required, distinguishing self-hosted wallets from unidentified ownership; and
  • correction, reconciliation and audit history.

FBR should receive tax information; PVARA should receive licensing, prudential and conduct information within its mandate. Section 17 of the VAA permits information sharing with FBR, but the exchange should be governed by a published legal instrument or controlled protocol specifying fields, purposes, security, retention, onward disclosure, corrections, access logging and responsible officers. PVARA need not receive every tax return, and FBR need not receive every cybersecurity alert. A common entity identifier and controlled cross-reference are better than indiscriminate database replication.

Taxpayer administration must permit correction. A customer should be able to obtain a machine-readable annual statement, challenge wrong identity or basis attribution, mark a self-transfer, supply off-platform cost evidence and receive a corrected report before assessment where practicable. FBR should publish how duplicates across VASPs, chain analytics and foreign CARF reports are reconciled. An address should not be attributed to a taxpayer solely because an analytics vendor assigns a probability score.

Sections 174 and 176 permit records and information demands, while section 216 protects tax information subject to statutory exceptions. Those powers require audit trails, role-based access and reasoned use. Data obtained for automatic exchange should remain limited to lawful tax purposes and protected against unauthorised disclosure. Enforcement must follow assessment, notice, evidence and appeal procedures; a reported gross transfer is not self-proving taxable income.252

11.7 Provincial Services Tax and Federal Coordination

Pakistan has no single national sales-tax answer for a VASP transaction. The Constitution reserves federal sales tax on goods and excludes sales tax on services from the relevant federal entry. The Sales Tax Act 1990 charges federal sales tax on taxable supplies of goods by a registered person in the course of taxable activity and on imported goods. Its definition of goods includes movable property but excludes actionable claims, money, stocks, shares and securities. Whether a particular virtual asset is a “good” cannot be resolved without classifying the legal rights; the Act contains no express virtual-asset taxonomy in the text searched.253

The service leg is usually more immediate. Exchange, brokerage, dealing commission, custody, administration, advice, platform access, data, software, validation support and management may fall within one or more provincial scheduled-service categories. Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan operate distinct services-tax laws and instruments. Their schedules, descriptions, rates, exemptions, registration thresholds, place-of-provision rules, reverse-charge rules and notifications must be checked for the period and facts. A federal VASP licence neither exempts a service nor determines the province entitled to tax it.254

The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Act illustrates the structure without supplying a nationwide answer. It taxes services listed in its schedule, contains origin and consumption rules, can impose reverse charge for services originating outside the Province or Pakistan, values in-kind consideration by reference to open-market value, and lists categories including financial, brokerage, commission, computer/software, digital or IT-based, online-marketplace and management services. Rates differ by scheduled category and have been amended. It would therefore be unsafe to select one label or rate for all VASP services without a ruling on the exact service and current instrument.255

Each transaction should be disaggregated into at least:

1. transfer of the underlying asset;

2. exchange or brokerage commission;

3. custody or safeguarding fee;

4. technology, data or platform fee;

5. advisory, management or staking commission; and

6. any imported or intercompany service.

Bundling does not make the components disappear. The contract and invoice should allocate consideration on an arm’s-length basis and identify the place and recipient of each service. Payment in tokens requires fair-value invoicing; it does not remove services tax.

Coordination should be administrative rather than constitutionally assimilative. FBR and the provincial authorities can agree a common taxpayer identifier, registration-status exchange, invoice fields, audit-coordination protocol and conflict-escalation route. A lead audit may collect evidence once, but each authority must issue any demand under its own competent law. Place-of-provision conflicts should have a rapid inter-authority determination process so that one service is not taxed by several provinces merely because the customer, server, office and wallet are in different places.

PVARA can require a licensee to maintain jurisdictional transaction and fee data and to attest compliance. It should not decide provincial tax liability or prescribe a uniform services-tax rate. The durable settlement is a federal-provincial protocol endorsed through the appropriate intergovernmental mechanism, with published data fields and preservation of each legislature’s competence.

11.8 Accounting, Audit and Financial Statements

Tax accounting and financial reporting answer different questions. The Companies Act 2017 requires companies to keep books and other records giving a true and fair view and covering receipts, payments, sales, purchases, assets and liabilities. Financial statements must give a true and fair view, comply with standards notified by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP), and follow the applicable Schedule. Auditors must work under adopted auditing standards, assess whether adequate records exist, reconcile the statements to those records and report whether the required view is given.256

The IFRS Interpretations Committee’s June 2019 agenda decision is important but narrow. For the cryptocurrency fact pattern it considered—a digital or virtual currency on a distributed ledger, not issued by a jurisdiction or other party and not giving rise to a contract between the holder and another party—the holding is not cash and not a financial asset. IAS 2 applies when it is held for sale in the ordinary course of business; otherwise IAS 38 applies. A commodity broker-trader within IAS 2 measures qualifying inventory at fair value less costs to sell. The decision also points to fair-value, judgement and subsequent-event disclosures.257

It does not establish that all digital tokens are IAS 38 intangibles. A tokenised share or debt instrument can create contractual or equity rights; a redeemable stablecoin can create an issuer claim; a platform balance can be a receivable; an issuer can owe future goods or services; and a custodian can hold a customer asset with a corresponding safeguarding or restitution obligation. Classification requires the contract, governing law and economic rights, followed by the applicable notified standard—potentially including IFRS 9, IAS 32, IFRS 15, IAS 2, IAS 37 or another standard.

The financial statements of a VASP or issuer should make the following legible:

  • proprietary assets separately from customer assets and any related safeguarding liability;
  • custody model, segregation, reuse or rehypothecation rights and insolvency exposure;
  • asset and liability classification and the reason for it;
  • valuation technique, principal market, price source, liquidity, restrictions and sensitivity;
  • revenue by principal/agent capacity and material service stream;
  • issuer redemption, reserve, performance and contingent obligations;
  • staking, lending, protocol, counterparty and concentration exposures;
  • related-party transactions, subsequent events, impairment and going-concern uncertainty; and
  • current and deferred tax positions and material uncertain tax treatments under the applicable framework.

On-chain evidence strengthens audit but does not complete it. A signed message can support control of a key; it does not prove legal title, beneficial ownership, absence of an undisclosed obligation or completeness of all wallets. Proof of reserves can show selected assets at a point in time; without complete customer liabilities, legal ownership, encumbrances, subsequent movement and independent controls it cannot establish solvency. The audit should reconcile customer-level subledgers to omnibus wallets, inspect terms and title, test key governance and access, confirm external custodians, assess valuation sources, search for omitted wallets and liabilities, and test movements before and after the reporting date.258

The accounting ledger should feed but not dictate the tax return. Reconciling items should identify different recognition timing, disallowed or capital expenditure, tax basis, unrealised accounting movements, withholding and services tax. A regulator should not require one “crypto accounting policy” across instruments with materially different rights.

11.9 CARF, DAC8 and International Tax Transparency

The OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) is an annual standardised automatic-exchange system for tax information. It is not a tax charge, a licensing regime or a declaration that every reported transfer is taxable. Its purpose is to give participating tax administrations consistent information about relevant crypto-asset activity that can escape conventional financial-account reporting.259

CARF places reporting and due-diligence duties on a Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Provider (RCASP): a person that, as a business, provides a service effectuating exchange transactions for or on behalf of customers, including by acting as counterparty or intermediary or by making available a trading platform. Jurisdictional nexus can arise through tax residence, incorporation coupled with reporting obligations, management, a regular place of business or a branch, subject to coordination rules that prevent duplicative reporting.

For reportable users and controlling persons, the standard collects identity, address, jurisdiction of residence, tax identification number and, for individuals, date of birth, subject to its detailed rules. The RCASP reports its own identity and annual aggregate information by asset type. Categories include acquisitions against fiat, disposals against fiat, exchanges for other relevant crypto-assets valued at fair market value, reportable retail payments, and other transfers, including transfers to wallet addresses not known to be associated with another service provider. Due diligence relies on valid self-certifications tested against AML/KYC and other information, with change-of-circumstance controls. Documentation and data must generally be retained for at least five years after the reporting period.260

That design has consequences for Pakistan. A domestic CARF law would need to define:

  • relevant crypto-assets, excluded central-bank digital currencies and specified electronic-money products, and the relationship with CRS financial assets;
  • RCASP activities and Pakistan nexus, including branches and duplicate-reporting relief;
  • reportable and excluded persons and controlling persons;
  • due-diligence, self-certification, reasonableness and change-of-circumstance duties;
  • transaction categories, valuation currency, aggregation, corrections and nil reporting;
  • record retention, audit, sanctions proportionate to culpability and a right of review;
  • confidentiality, permitted use, data-subject correction and cybersecurity controls; and
  • FBR’s authority to receive, validate, exchange and protect the information.

PVARA should support the perimeter by giving FBR authoritative licence, service, branch and legal-person data. FBR should own tax reporting, due-diligence interpretation and international exchange. Joint rules should map PVARA’s “VASP” categories to CARF’s function-based “RCASP” test; the terms overlap but are not necessarily coextensive.

International exchange requires more than domestic data collection. The CARF Multilateral Competent Authority Agreement (MCAA) operates on the underlying Convention or another valid exchange basis and requires notifications concerning domestic implementing law and commencement, reciprocal status, permitted use, transmission and encryption, personal-data safeguards, confidentiality and intended exchange partners. A bilateral exchange relationship becomes active only after both competent authorities have completed the specified steps and listed each other. Information-security and sanction controls are substantive preconditions, not launch-day paperwork.261

The OECD Global Forum’s official commitment list, last updated 23 June 2026, names 46 jurisdictions undertaking first exchanges by 2027, 29 by 2028, the United States by 2029, and five relevant jurisdictions not yet committed. Pakistan does not appear on that list. The narrow conclusion is that no Pakistan commitment is evidenced by that document as at its stated date. It does not establish rejection, prevent a later commitment or prove that domestic preparatory work has not occurred.262

Pakistan should use a staged path:

1. perform a legal and data-gap assessment against the CARF rules and XML schema;

2. enact primary authority and rules only after defining scope, safeguards, sanctions and appeal;

3. register and map RCASPs using PVARA and FBR data;

4. run controlled test reporting with synthetic and then reconciled historical data;

5. obtain an independent confidentiality and information-security assessment;

6. sign or activate the relevant international instrument and make the required notifications;

7. select exchange partners only after reciprocal legal and safeguard checks; and

8. begin production with correction, duplicate-suppression and taxpayer access mechanisms.

The European Union’s DAC8 is adjacent but distinct. According to the European Commission, its crypto-asset reporting rules apply from 1 January 2026, with reporting for 2026 and exchange by 30 September 2027. It covers domestic and cross-border reportable activity and can require a non-EU crypto-asset operator not authorised under MiCA to register in one Member State. DAC8 is not Pakistani law and does not confer a Pakistan licence. It matters operationally where a Pakistan-connected provider has EU-reportable users or an EU registration obligation, and because its data fields should be mapped to CARF to avoid incompatible duplicative systems.263

Transparency must remain proportionate. A foreign report can be wrong, duplicated or based on a different residence determination. FBR should match reports to taxpayers using more than a name, notify material use where law requires, permit correction and assess tax under Pakistan’s charging provisions. CARF should close information gaps; it should not convert gross flows into presumed concealed income.

11.10 Public Revenue, Compliance Cost and Forecasting

The VAA creates a lapsable PVARA Fund and identifies sources including Government grants, licence and supervision fees, fines, penalties, service charges and other receipts. It subjects the Fund to the Public Finance Management Act 2019, requires budgeting and accounts, and provides for Auditor-General and chartered-accountant audit and annual reporting. The public-finance statute requires self-generated revenue of public entities to enter the Treasury Single Account, requires non-tax revenue to be levied under relevant law, directs collection into the Federal Consolidated Fund, and prevents retention or appropriation outside the constitutional budget mechanism.264

Three fiscal rules follow. First, licence and supervisory fees should recover the efficient cost of regulation and reflect risk or activity where law permits; they should not operate as disguised taxes. Second, penalties should deter and correct misconduct, not become a budget target that rewards enforcement volume. Third, PVARA cannot treat the gross receipts named in section 14 as an independent spending authority.

Revenue forecasting must reject gross trading volume as a tax base. Volume includes acquisitions, self-transfers, market-making turnover, crypto-to-crypto exchanges, wash activity, losses and customer assets that are not VASP income. A defensible annual model is:

> Net fiscal yield = Σ[(realised taxable base by income head × effective rate) + (taxable service-fee base by province × applicable rate)] × compliance-and-collection factor − lawful credits, refunds and loss offsets − incremental administration and compliance cost.

The model should publish low, central and high cases for active taxpayers, realised gains and losses, business margins, fee take-rates, provincial allocation, cost-basis completeness, voluntary compliance, audit yield, bad debt, refunds and implementation cost. No Rupee forecast is credible until FBR and the Provincial Authorities can distinguish customer flow from taxable income and can reconcile basis across domestic, self-hosted and foreign accounts.265

Administrative cost includes FBR and provincial system development, data security, specialist valuation and audit capacity, dispute resolution, taxpayer support, international-exchange testing and independent assurance. Private compliance cost includes identity and residence refresh, valuation, statement correction, systems integration and retention. Rules should permit simplified valuation and aggregated reporting for genuinely low-risk retail activity while preserving transaction-level records, and should provide safe correction before penalties for reasonable first-year errors.

The fiscal dashboard should report registrations, timely and corrected reports, unmatched records, basis completeness, assessment yield net of reversals, refund delay, appeal outcomes, security incidents, cost per usable report and taxpayer-support resolution. A high volume of data or penalties is not evidence of an effective tax system.

11.11 Statutory Defect and Corrective Package

Pakistan’s current position is neither a tax vacuum nor a complete digital-asset tax regime. General federal and provincial rules can reach many receipts, gains and services. Yet the operative texts inspected do not expressly classify virtual assets, resolve the personal-use movable-property problem, prescribe a cost-basis convention, convert crypto-to-crypto and in-kind events into a consistent reporting rule, create general VASP withholding, or implement CARF. Section 66 acknowledges tax compliance while leaving those questions untouched and naming the principal income-tax enactment incorrectly.266

The corrective package should proceed in the following order.

1. Repair section 66. Replace “Income Tax Act, 2001” with “Income Tax Ordinance, 2001” and refer, without pre-empting provincial competence, to applicable federal and provincial tax laws. State expressly that the section does not itself impose a tax, exemption or withholding obligation. Preserve FBR and Provincial Revenue Authority powers under their own enactments.

2. Enact a technology-neutral income-tax taxonomy. Define “virtual asset” for tax purposes by reference to transferable digital value or rights using cryptographically secured distributed-ledger or similar technology, while coordinating exclusions for fiat currency, central-bank digital currency and instruments already governed as securities or other property. The definition should route an asset to the existing head determined by its rights and use; it should not create one universal “crypto income” category.

3. Specify events, basis and valuation. Confirm the treatment of fiat sales, exchanges for another asset, purchases of goods or services, rewards, airdrops, forks, wrapped assets, migrations, gifts, death, loss and same-owner wallet transfers. Select a consistent cost-basis method, permit documented specific identification where administrable, address lost or inaccessible assets, and prescribe an FMV hierarchy, timestamp, Rupee conversion path and related-party rule. Parliament should decide whether and how the section 37 personal-use movable-property exclusion applies to virtual assets.

4. Separate asset taxation from services tax. FBR should issue federal guidance on the “goods” question only within the Sales Tax Act 1990. The Provinces should classify exchange, custody, brokerage, technology, advice and related services under their own laws. A federal-provincial protocol should supply common invoice and data fields, place-of-provision conflict handling and coordinated audits without reallocating legislative competence.

5. Create proportionate domestic reporting before withholding. Require annual machine-readable statements, event and valuation fields, customer access, correction and six-year minimum records, coordinated with longer company-law retention. Do not impose blanket gross-proceeds withholding. Any withholding must identify the taxable payment, rate, credit mechanism, in-kind funding procedure, loss treatment and appeal.

6. Build CARF through tax law. Amend the Ordinance or enact competent primary provisions defining RCASPs, reportable persons and transactions, due diligence, valuation, records, confidentiality, sanctions and review. Authorise FBR as competent tax administrator and international exchange body; require PVARA to provide verified perimeter and licence data. Complete the MCAA, notification, information-security and bilateral-activation steps only after domestic testing.

7. Align accounting and tax reconciliation. SECP, in consultation with ICAP, FBR and PVARA, should publish rights-based application guidance rather than a universal token classification. Licensed entities should disclose customer-asset treatment, safeguarding obligations, valuation, principal/agent revenue and tax-reconciliation controls. Audit guidance should reject proof of reserves as a substitute for complete assets, liabilities, title and controls.

8. Protect public money and measure net yield. Place fees and penalties through the PFM framework, publish cost-recovery principles, report gross and net regulatory receipts, and prohibit enforcement revenue targets. Finance Division and tax authorities should publish scenario assumptions and implementation cost before relying on digital assets in a medium-term revenue forecast.

The sequence matters. Reporting before classification produces large but ambiguous datasets. Withholding before basis rules taxes turnover rather than income. International exchange before correction and security controls exports errors and risk. A durable fiscal regime instead begins with lawful incidence, converts rights and events into reproducible records, gives each authority only the information and power it needs, and subjects revenue itself to public law.

That is the fiscal meaning of the report’s governing thesis. Code can show that value moved. Accounting can represent what an entity controls or owes. Reporting can tell a tax administration where to enquire. None can answer the constitutional question—who may impose what burden, on whom and under which law—without legislation whose authority, base and remedy remain legible.

---

Working-Draft Apparatus

Substantive status: Complete working draft of sections 11.1–11.11, including constitutional competence; the taxpayer-character-timing-value-source-reporting-uncertainty event matrix; federal income and goods-tax analysis; provincial services-tax coordination; valuation, basis, timing and records; actor-specific treatment; withholding and administration; accounting and audit; CARF and DAC8; public-finance controls; revenue sensitivity; and the corrective statutory package. It is not publication-ready until Author review, whole-manuscript editorial integration and rendered design review are complete.

Evidence status: Relevant provisions of the official Virtual Assets Act 2026, Constitution, Income Tax Ordinance 2001 amended to 30 June 2026, Sales Tax Act 1990 amended to 30 June 2026, Companies Act 2017, Public Finance Management Act 2019 and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa services-tax statute were textually read and their material PDF pages visually inspected. The OECD CARF standard, MCAA and 23 June 2026 commitment list and the IFRIC agenda decision were textually read and visually checked. Current official federal, provincial, OECD and European Commission pages were checked through 16 August 2026. The documented negative search did not locate an express virtual-asset taxonomy in the principal federal tax texts searched; that limit is not represented as proof that no subordinate instrument or ruling exists.

Citation status: Footnote sequence 239–266 continues the canonical manuscript after Chapter 10. Final Author reading, current-Gazette and provincial-notification verification, taxpayer-specific treaty analysis, pinpoint review, link check and whole-manuscript citation clearance remain pending.

Cross-chapter transfers: cybersecurity, personal data, digital identity, regulatory reporting and electronic evidence → Chapter 12; smart contracts, DeFi, DAOs, oracles and autonomous agents → Chapter 13; institutional staffing, intergovernmental delivery capacity, mining, electricity, land and environmental coordination → Chapter 14; assessment, investigation, penalties, adjudication, appeals and remedies → Chapter 15; sustained comparative tax and reporting design → Chapter 16; consolidated statutory language and implementation sequencing → Chapter 17.

-The securities legislation already regulates advisers, brokers and managers; customer assets; public offers and prospectuses; insider trading; and manipulation and fraud. The futures legislation licenses exchanges and regulated activities, protects customer assets, and prohibits insider dealing, false trading and manipulation.[^c11-1]
-[OPERATIVE] The Act nonetheless vests primary authority over the tokenisation of real-world assets in the Authority,[^c11-2] and creates its own market-abuse and insider concepts.[^c11-3] For assets outside the securities perimeter that is legitimate and necessary. For tokenised securities it produces two regimes over one instrument.
-### 11.2 What the double regime costs
-An issuer of an asset-backed token faces a choice between two disclosure documents drafted to different standards; two custody regimes with different segregation mechanics; two market-abuse codes with different definitions of inside information; and two enforcement authorities either of which may reach a finding the other does not share. That is not conservative regulation. It is a licence to arb
-### 11.3 The classification gateway again
-The remedy is the one proposed at Chapter 5: an instrument satisfying the definition of a security remains a security, and the securities regulator remains its regulator, irrespective of the ledger on which it is represented. The Authority's role over such an instrument is confined to the additional technological layer, exercised under joint regulations that name the lead regulator.
-Anything short of that leaves the boundary to be litigated by a market participant who cannot afford to litigate.
-### 11.4 The issuer gap
-[GAP] Only Pakistan-registered entities may conduct an initial token offering, and marketing is prohibited unless the issuer holds a licence or registration under the Act.[^c11-4] But the licensing machinery is framed around service providers and enumerated third-party services. Schedule I's issuance-services category may capture a provider assisting an issuance; it does not obviously make the pr
-The result is a *casus omissus* of an unusually serious kind: the Act creates an offence whose element is the absence of a status it never provides a route to obtain. Regulations may administer a statutory regime; they should not create the essential licence, the offence-triggering status and the regulator's discretion from nothing.
-**The cure**: enact a dedicated issuer chapter, or expressly apply specified licensing provisions to issuers with necessary modifications, and coordinate tokenised-security offers with prospectus approval under the securities legislation.
-### 11.5 Winding up
-[OPERATIVE] On revocation of a licence, the Authority must notify the corporate regulator to initiate winding up or dissolution.[^c11-5] [GAP] But the company legislation defines the grounds for winding up and who may petition; a notification from another regulator is neither a ground nor an order, and the corporate regulator's petitioning route may depend on its own statutory preconditions.[^c11
-There is also a policy problem beneath the technical one. Revocation of a virtual-asset licence should not automatically destroy a solvent company that can cease the regulated business, transfer its customers safely and continue lawful operations. The corrective bill should create an explicit petition ground with standing, while preserving court discretion, creditor and customer notice, and wind-

+## 11.1 The Fiscal Question and Constitutional Competence
+Digital-asset taxation begins with legality, not with a policy desire to capture revenue. Article 77 of the Constitution permits a federal tax only by or under an Act of Parliament. Article 142 and the Federal Legislative List then allocate legislative competence: the Federation has the listed fields, including taxes on income other than agricultural income, taxes on corporations, taxes on sales
+Section 66 of the *Virtual Assets Act 2026* does not alter that position. It directs licensed virtual-asset service providers (VASPs) to comply with obligations under the “Income Tax Act, 2001” and rules and regulations made by the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR). The operative federal enactment is the *Income Tax Ordinance, 2001*, not an “Income Tax Act, 2001”. More fundamentally, section 66 name
+That conclusion does not make virtual-asset activity tax free. The general charging and computational rules of the *Income Tax Ordinance 2001* can apply where their elements are satisfied. It means only that the legal work cannot be skipped. For each transaction the enquiry must identify: **the person taxed; the event recognised; the character of the amount; its timing and Rupee value; the source
+Four systems must also remain separate. **Tax law** determines liability. **Tax reporting** supplies information relevant to assessment and exchange. **Financial reporting** represents assets, liabilities, income, expenses and uncertainty under the applicable accounting framework. **Public-finance law** determines where public receipts are deposited, appropriated, audited and reported. The same t
+The controlling fiscal principle is therefore modest but exacting: technology may change the evidence and the transaction path, but only competent legislation can change the incidence of tax.
+## 11.2 Asset and Income Classification, and the Taxable Event
+The *Income Tax Ordinance 2001* taxes income through recognised heads. Total income is constructed from the heads of salary, income from property, income from business, capital gains and income from other sources. For digital assets, the principal contest is usually among business income under section 18, capital gain under section 37, and residual or specifically included income under section 39
+A dealing business, market maker, broker-trader, miner operating commercially, validator service, issuer or enterprise disposing of inventory may have business receipts and allowable business expenditure under the ordinary rules. An investor disposing of property may fall within capital gains. A reward, distribution or property received without consideration may require analysis under business in
+The capital-gains route contains an important qualification. Section 37 defines a capital asset as property of any kind held by a person, whether or not connected with business, but excludes stock-in-trade, depreciable or amortisable property and—subject to the collectible categories in section 38—movable property held for personal use. Section 37A separately governs specified “securities”; a vir
+Sections 75–78 supply a wider transaction grammar. Disposal includes sale, exchange, transfer, distribution, cancellation, redemption, relinquishment, destruction, loss, expiry or surrender; acquisition begins when ownership or the relevant right begins. Cost includes consideration—using fair market value for consideration in kind—incidental acquisition and disposal expenditure, and improvements.

+## 11.3 Residence, Source and Cross-Border Activity
+Distributed infrastructure does not abolish tax residence or geographical source. The Ordinance determines residence separately for individuals, companies and associations of persons. +## 11.4 Valuation, Basis, Timing and Records
+Volatility is not the legal reason valuation is difficult. The deeper problem is that “price” can refer to an order-book quote, executed trade, index, oracle, thin-liquidity pool, related-party transfer, locked token, redeemable claim or manipulated market. Section 68 uses an open-market fair-market-value standard and permits the Commissioner to determine value where it is not ordinarily ascertai
+A defensible methodology should apply a hierarchy:
+1. use the actual arm’s-length transaction price on a reliable venue where it represents the rights transferred;
+2. where that price is unavailable or distorted, use a documented volume-weighted or time-consistent composite from independent liquid venues;
+3. value a redeemable claim by reference to enforceable redemption rights only after testing issuer credit, reserve access, fees, delay and restrictions;
+4. for illiquid, vested, locked or rights-bearing tokens, apply an appropriate valuation technique and disclose restrictions, assumptions and uncertainty; and
+5. where no reliable value can be established, preserve the evidence, state the uncertainty and use the statutory determination route rather than inventing precision.
+The policy must fix a consistent valuation time and time zone. A daily closing price is administratively simple but can be arbitrary for intraday exchanges. Exact transaction-time valuation is more accurate but costly for high-frequency activity. A proportionate rule can require actual executed value where available, allow a prescribed daily method for qualifying retail volumes, and require trans
+Section 71 converts foreign currency and Rupees at the State Bank rate on the relevant date; it does not classify every crypto-asset as foreign currency. A sound rule would establish fair value in reliable fiat and then translate it into Rupees at the lawful State Bank rate.

Each taxpayer should maintain, at minimum: acquisition date and time; quantity and asset identifier; chain and contract address where relevant; legal rights; wallet or account; counterparty or venue; consideration and incidental fees; valuation source; transaction identifier; beneficial owner; tax character; transfer history; and disposal proceeds. +## 11.5 Treatment by Actor and Function
+Tax classification should follow the actor’s function and the rights created. A single organisation may perform several functions, and each stream may have a different base.
+**Individuals and investors.** Frequency, organisation, intention, financing, holding period, use of specialised systems and relation to an existing business can inform whether activity is a business or investment, but no single factor should be treated as conclusive. A holder must separately identify acquisitions, disposals, income rewards and personal-use assertions. Wealth-statement and foreig
+**VASPs.** An exchange may earn trading commissions, spreads, listing fees, custody fees, withdrawal fees, staking commissions, data revenue and gains or losses on proprietary inventory. Customer gross trading volume is not the VASP’s income. Customer assets held without beneficial title should not be booked or taxed as the custodian’s own property merely because the custodian controls private ke
+**Brokers, dealers and market makers.** A person trading as principal may hold stock-in-trade and recognise business profits; an agent ordinarily recognises commission rather than the customer’s gross consideration. A platform acting as both principal and agent must disclose the capacity in each transaction and prevent internal pricing from shifting profit between related entities or jurisdiction
+**Issuers.** Token issuance is not one tax event. A sale can represent an immediate supply, advance consideration for future performance, a borrowing or redeemable liability, a membership or governance right, an equity-like interest, a bundled arrangement or a transfer of property. Income recognition, deductions and sales-tax treatment follow the enforceable rights and performance obligations. Tr
+**Miners and validators.** Commercial block-production or validation rewards may be business income, with ordinary-law treatment of allowable expenses. The legal recipient must be distinguished from pool operator, delegator and infrastructure host. Validator commission and delegator reward can have different character; later disposal is a separate event using the recognition value as basis.
+**Staking, lending and decentralised-finance arrangements.** Labels such as “yield”, “interest”, “liquidity mining” or “staking” do not determine character. The enquiry asks whether the taxpayer transferred title, lent property, supplied a service, entered a partnership-like arrangement, received compensation for risk, disposed of one right for another, or merely delegated validation power. Proto
+**Custodians and fiduciaries.** The tax and accounting result turns on customer title, segregation, reuse rights, insolvency treatment, restitution obligation and beneficial entitlement. If terms permit the custodian to use assets and return an equivalent, the arrangement may be economically and legally closer to a loan than a bailment or safeguarding service. If title remains with the customer,
+**Companies, funds, trusts and estates.** Entity form, tax status and governing instrument matter. A company does not receive individual personal-use treatment. A fund or trust requires identification of the taxable person, beneficiaries and distributions. On death, the legal representative must secure wallet access and preserve basis; inheritance and later disposal are separate. The VAA creates
+Actor-based rules should remain technology neutral but not evidence blind. They should require the information peculiar to virtual assets—wallets, contract rights, keys, transaction identifiers, chain events and venue pricing—only because those facts help apply the legal categories.

+## 11.7 Provincial Services Tax and Federal Coordination
+Pakistan has no single national sales-tax answer for a VASP transaction. The Constitution reserves federal sales tax on goods and excludes sales tax on services from the relevant federal entry. The *Sales Tax Act 1990* charges federal sales tax on taxable supplies of goods by a registered person in the course of taxable activity and on imported goods. Its definition of goods includes movable prop
+The service leg is usually more immediate. Exchange, brokerage, dealing commission, custody, administration, advice, platform access, data, software, validation support and management may fall within one or more provincial scheduled-service categories. Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan operate distinct services-tax laws and instruments. Their schedules, descriptions, rates, exempt
+The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Act illustrates the structure without supplying a nationwide answer. It taxes services listed in its schedule, contains origin and consumption rules, can impose reverse charge for services originating outside the Province or Pakistan, values in-kind consideration by reference to open-market value, and lists categories including financial, brokerage, commission, computer/sof
+Each transaction should be disaggregated into at least:
+1. transfer of the underlying asset;
+2. exchange or brokerage commission;
+3. custody or safeguarding fee;
+4. technology, data or platform fee;
+5. advisory, management or staking commission; and
+6. any imported or intercompany service.
+Bundling does not make the components disappear. The contract and invoice should allocate consideration on an arm’s-length basis and identify the place and recipient of each service. Payment in tokens requires fair-value invoicing; it does not remove services tax.
+Coordination should be administrative rather than constitutionally assimilative. FBR and the provincial authorities can agree a common taxpayer identifier, registration-status exchange, invoice fields, audit-coordination protocol and conflict-escalation route. A lead audit may collect evidence once, but each authority must issue any demand under its own competent law. Place-of-provision conflicts
+PVARA can require a licensee to maintain jurisdictional transaction and fee data and to attest compliance. It should not decide provincial tax liability or prescribe a uniform services-tax rate. The durable settlement is a federal-provincial protocol endorsed through the appropriate intergovernmental mechanism, with published data fields and preservation of each legislature’s competence.
+## 11.8 Accounting, Audit and Financial Statements
+Tax accounting and financial reporting answer different questions. The *Companies Act 2017* requires companies to keep books and other records giving a true and fair view and covering receipts, payments, sales, purchases, assets and liabilities. Financial statements must give a true and fair view, comply with standards notified by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP), and fol
+The IFRS Interpretations Committee’s June 2019 agenda decision is important but narrow. For the cryptocurrency fact pattern it considered—a digital or virtual currency on a distributed ledger, not issued by a jurisdiction or other party and not giving rise to a contract between the holder and another party—the holding is not cash and not a financial asset. IAS 2 applies when it is held for sale i
+It does not establish that all digital tokens are IAS 38 intangibles. A tokenised share or debt instrument can create contractual or equity rights; a redeemable stablecoin can create an issuer claim; a platform balance can be a receivable; an issuer can owe future goods or services; and a custodian can hold a customer asset with a corresponding safeguarding or restitution obligation. Classificati
+The financial statements of a VASP or issuer should make the following legible:
+- proprietary assets separately from customer assets and any related safeguarding liability;
+- custody model, segregation, reuse or rehypothecation rights and insolvency exposure;
+- asset and liability classification and the reason for it;
+- valuation technique, principal market, price source, liquidity, restrictions and sensitivity;
+- revenue by principal/agent capacity and material service stream;
+- issuer redemption, reserve, performance and contingent obligations;
+- staking, lending, protocol, counterparty and concentration exposures;
+- related-party transactions, subsequent events, impairment and going-concern uncertainty; and
+- current and deferred tax positions and material uncertain tax treatments under the applicable framework.
+On-chain evidence strengthens audit but does not complete it. A signed message can support control of a key; it does not prove legal title, beneficial ownership, absence of an undisclosed obligation or completeness of all wallets. Proof of reserves can show selected assets at a point in time; without complete customer liabilities, legal ownership, encumbrances, subsequent movement and independent
+The accounting ledger should feed but not dictate the tax return. Reconciling items should identify different recognition timing, disallowed or capital expenditure, tax basis, unrealised accounting movements, withholding and services tax. A regulator should not require one “crypto accounting policy” across instruments with materially different rights.
+## 11.9 CARF, DAC8 and International Tax Transparency
+The OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) is an annual standardised automatic-exchange system for tax information. It is not a tax charge, a licensing regime or a declaration that every reported transfer is taxable. Its purpose is to give participating tax administrations consistent information about relevant crypto-asset activity that can escape conventional financial-account reporting.[^
+CARF places reporting and due-diligence duties on a Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Provider (RCASP): a person that, as a business, provides a service effectuating exchange transactions for or on behalf of customers, including by acting as counterparty or intermediary or by making available a trading platform. Jurisdictional nexus can arise through tax residence, incorporation coupled with reporti
+For reportable users and controlling persons, the standard collects identity, address, jurisdiction of residence, tax identification number and, for individuals, date of birth, subject to its detailed rules. The RCASP reports its own identity and annual aggregate information by asset type. Categories include acquisitions against fiat, disposals against fiat, exchanges for other relevant crypto-as
+That design has consequences for Pakistan. A domestic CARF law would need to define:
+- relevant crypto-assets, excluded central-bank digital currencies and specified electronic-money products, and the relationship with CRS financial assets;
+- RCASP activities and Pakistan nexus, including branches and duplicate-reporting relief;
+- reportable and excluded persons and controlling persons;
+- due-diligence, self-certification, reasonableness and change-of-circumstance duties;
+- transaction categories, valuation currency, aggregation, corrections and nil reporting;
+- record retention, audit, sanctions proportionate to culpability and a right of review;
+- confidentiality, permitted use, data-subject correction and cybersecurity controls; and
+- FBR’s authority to receive, validate, exchange and protect the information.
+PVARA should support the perimeter by giving FBR authoritative licence, service, branch and legal-person data. FBR should own tax reporting, due-diligence interpretation and international exchange. Joint rules should map PVARA’s “VASP” categories to CARF’s function-based “RCASP” test; the terms overlap but are not necessarily coextensive.
+International exchange requires more than domestic data collection. The CARF Multilateral Competent Authority Agreement (MCAA) operates on the underlying Convention or another valid exchange basis and requires notifications concerning domestic implementing law and commencement, reciprocal status, permitted use, transmission and encryption, personal-data safeguards, confidentiality and intended ex
+The OECD Global Forum’s official commitment list, last updated 23 June 2026, names 46 jurisdictions undertaking first exchanges by 2027, 29 by 2028, the United States by 2029, and five relevant jurisdictions not yet committed. Pakistan does not appear on that list. The narrow conclusion is that no Pakistan commitment is evidenced by that document as at its stated date. It does not establish rejec
+Pakistan should use a staged path:
+1. perform a legal and data-gap assessment against the CARF rules and XML schema;
+2. enact primary authority and rules only after defining scope, safeguards, sanctions and appeal;
+3. register and map RCASPs using PVARA and FBR data;
+4. run controlled test reporting with synthetic and then reconciled historical data;
+5. obtain an independent confidentiality and information-security assessment;
+6. sign or activate the relevant international instrument and make the required notifications;
+7. select exchange partners only after reciprocal legal and safeguard checks; and
+8. begin production with correction, duplicate-suppression and taxpayer access mechanisms.
+The European Union’s DAC8 is adjacent but distinct. According to the European Commission, its crypto-asset reporting rules apply from 1 January 2026, with reporting for 2026 and exchange by 30 September 2027. It covers domestic and cross-border reportable activity and can require a non-EU crypto-asset operator not authorised under MiCA to register in one Member State. DAC8 is not Pakistani law an
+Transparency must remain proportionate. A foreign report can be wrong, duplicated or based on a different residence determination. FBR should match reports to taxpayers using more than a name, notify material use where law requires, permit correction and assess tax under Pakistan’s charging provisions. CARF should close information gaps; it should not convert gross flows into presumed concealed i
+## 11.10 Public Revenue, Compliance Cost and Forecasting
+The VAA creates a lapsable PVARA Fund and identifies sources including Government grants, licence and supervision fees, fines, penalties, service charges and other receipts. It subjects the Fund to the *Public Finance Management Act 2019*, requires budgeting and accounts, and provides for Auditor-General and chartered-accountant audit and annual reporting. The public-finance statute requires self
+Three fiscal rules follow. First, licence and supervisory fees should recover the efficient cost of regulation and reflect risk or activity where law permits; they should not operate as disguised taxes. Second, penalties should deter and correct misconduct, not become a budget target that rewards enforcement volume. Third, PVARA cannot treat the gross receipts named in section 14 as an independen
+Revenue forecasting must reject gross trading volume as a tax base. Volume includes acquisitions, self-transfers, market-making turnover, crypto-to-crypto exchanges, wash activity, losses and customer assets that are not VASP income. A defensible annual model is:
+> **Net fiscal yield = Σ[(realised taxable base by income head × effective rate) + (taxable service-fee base by province × applicable rate)] × compliance-and-collection factor − lawful credits, refunds and loss offsets − incremental administration and compliance cost.**
+The model should publish low, central and high cases for active taxpayers, realised gains and losses, business margins, fee take-rates, provincial allocation, cost-basis completeness, voluntary compliance, audit yield, bad debt, refunds and implementation cost. No Rupee forecast is credible until FBR and the Provincial Authorities can distinguish customer flow from taxable income and can reconcil
+Administrative cost includes FBR and provincial system development, data security, specialist valuation and audit capacity, dispute resolution, taxpayer support, international-exchange testing and independent assurance. Private compliance cost includes identity and residence refresh, valuation, statement correction, systems integration and retention. Rules should permit simplified valuation and a
+The fiscal dashboard should report registrations, timely and corrected reports, unmatched records, basis completeness, assessment yield net of reversals, refund delay, appeal outcomes, security incidents, cost per usable report and taxpayer-support resolution. A high volume of data or penalties is not evidence of an effective tax system.
+## 11.11 Statutory Defect and Corrective Package
+Pakistan’s current position is neither a tax vacuum nor a complete digital-asset tax regime. General federal and provincial rules can reach many receipts, gains and services. Chapter 11 — Taxation, CARF, Accounting and Public Finance

Chapter status: SUBSTANTIVE WORKING DRAFT — AUTHOR REVIEW AND FINAL CITATION CLEARANCE PENDING

Evidence cut-off for this chapter: 16 August 2026

11.1 The Fiscal Question and Constitutional Competence

Digital-asset taxation begins with legality, not with a policy desire to capture revenue. Article 77 of the Constitution permits a federal tax only by or under an Act of Parliament. Article 142 and the Federal Legislative List then allocate legislative competence: the Federation has the listed fields, including taxes on income other than agricultural income, taxes on corporations, taxes on sales and purchases of goods other than sales tax on services, and taxes on the capital value of assets subject to the constitutional text; the Provinces retain the service-tax field. A regulator cannot turn licensing guidance, a circular, a reporting form or an information-sharing agreement into a tax charge that Parliament or a competent Provincial Legislature did not enact.239

Section 66 of the Virtual Assets Act 2026 does not alter that position. It directs licensed virtual-asset service providers (VASPs) to comply with obligations under the “Income Tax Act, 2001” and rules and regulations made by the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR). The operative federal enactment is the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, not an “Income Tax Act, 2001”. More fundamentally, section 66 names no taxpayer, taxable event, head of income, rate, tax base, valuation rule, source rule or withholding mechanism. It is a compliance bridge with a defective statutory citation, not an independent charge to tax.240

That conclusion does not make virtual-asset activity tax free. The general charging and computational rules of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001 can apply where their elements are satisfied. It means only that the legal work cannot be skipped. For each transaction the enquiry must identify: the person taxed; the event recognised; the character of the amount; its timing and Rupee value; the source and residence nexus; the deductions, losses or reliefs permitted; the return or third-party report required; and the authority for collection or enforcement.

Four systems must also remain separate. Tax law determines liability. Tax reporting supplies information relevant to assessment and exchange. Financial reporting represents assets, liabilities, income, expenses and uncertainty under the applicable accounting framework. Public-finance law determines where public receipts are deposited, appropriated, audited and reported. The same transfer can enter all four systems, but a reporting entry is not a tax assessment; an accounting fair value is not automatically the statutory tax value; and a fee collected by PVARA is not money available for expenditure outside the constitutional budget process.

The controlling fiscal principle is therefore modest but exacting: technology may change the evidence and the transaction path, but only competent legislation can change the incidence of tax.

11.2 Asset and Income Classification, and the Taxable Event

The Income Tax Ordinance 2001 taxes income through recognised heads. Total income is constructed from the heads of salary, income from property, income from business, capital gains and income from other sources. For digital assets, the principal contest is usually among business income under section 18, capital gain under section 37, and residual or specifically included income under section 39. The answer depends on the taxpayer’s activity and rights, not on a platform’s product label.241

A dealing business, market maker, broker-trader, miner operating commercially, validator service, issuer or enterprise disposing of inventory may have business receipts and allowable business expenditure under the ordinary rules. An investor disposing of property may fall within capital gains. A reward, distribution or property received without consideration may require analysis under business income or income from other sources. Salary or professional remuneration paid in tokens retains its underlying employment or service character; the payment medium does not move it into capital gains.

The capital-gains route contains an important qualification. Section 37 defines a capital asset as property of any kind held by a person, whether or not connected with business, but excludes stock-in-trade, depreciable or amortisable property and—subject to the collectible categories in section 38—movable property held for personal use. Section 37A separately governs specified “securities”; a virtual asset is not brought within that special regime merely because a commercial platform calls it a security token. Consequently, it would be unsafe to state that every retail token disposal generates a taxable capital gain. Where an individual establishes genuine personal use, the movable-property exclusion may disapply the section 37 capital-gain route, leaving a classification gap or another head-of-income question that requires statutory resolution.242

Sections 75–78 supply a wider transaction grammar. Disposal includes sale, exchange, transfer, distribution, cancellation, redemption, relinquishment, destruction, loss, expiry or surrender; acquisition begins when ownership or the relevant right begins. Cost includes consideration—using fair market value for consideration in kind—incidental acquisition and disposal expenditure, and improvements. Consideration on disposal is generally the amount received or fair market value, whichever is higher, with non-arm’s-length transactions tested at fair market value. Those rules mean that a crypto-to-crypto exchange or purchase of goods with a token can contain a disposal even though no Rupees pass through a bank.243

Gifts and succession illustrate why technical transfer and tax recognition are not synonymous. Section 75 can describe an ownership event, while section 79 can require no gain or loss and preserve character and cost in qualifying transfers, including transmission on death and specified gifts. A 2026 cost rule for inherited immovable property does not supply a corresponding virtual-asset fair-value step-up. Executors therefore need the deceased’s original acquisition, wallet and control records; a market quotation at death cannot by itself replace the statutory cost rule.244

The matrix is not a schedule of new taxes. It is a discipline for applying existing law and exposing the places where Parliament, FBR or a Provincial Legislature must speak more clearly.

11.3 Residence, Source and Cross-Border Activity

Distributed infrastructure does not abolish tax residence or geographical source. The Ordinance determines residence separately for individuals, companies and associations of persons. It then brings into a resident person’s total income the Pakistan-source and foreign-source amounts within the statutory framework, while a non-resident is generally within the charge for Pakistan-source income. Treaty relief, foreign-tax credit, exemptions and special regimes may modify the result; they do not permit residence to be inferred from an IP address or exchange location.245

For a resident business, section 101 treats business income as Pakistan-source to the extent derived from business carried on in Pakistan. For a non-resident, attribution may arise through a permanent establishment, sales through such establishment, a business connection or other specified connections. Gains on assets used in a relevant business, services, royalties, profit on debt and other categories have their own source rules. A virtual-asset analysis should therefore begin with the person and the income-producing activity: where management occurs; who contracts; where personnel and systems perform the service; whether an agent or permanent establishment acts; where rights and obligations are situated; and to what Pakistan activity income is attributable.

Section 101’s 2024 “significant economic presence” provisions extend the business-connection enquiry to prescribed levels of transactions in goods, services or property, including downloads of data or software, and to systematic and continuous interaction through digital means with a prescribed number of users in Pakistan. The text is relevant to foreign exchanges and platforms, but it is not a licence to tax global income by counting Pakistani app visits. The monetary or user threshold must be prescribed and met, a business connection must arise under the section, and only income attributable to the Pakistan connection is brought within the source rule.246

Certain attractive proxies are legally weak. The location of validating nodes does not necessarily identify the seller, service provider or owner. The situs of a private key says little where a cloud custodian, multisignature group or recovery provider participates. A domain name, downloadable app or Pakistani customer may support an evidential nexus, but none replaces the statutory source test. Conversely, a foreign-incorporated platform with management, personnel, agents or sustained service operations in Pakistan cannot defeat the source enquiry merely by settling transactions on a borderless ledger.

The minimum cross-border file should record:

  • taxpayer residence and the legal basis for it;
  • counterparty and beneficial-owner identity where required and obtainable;
  • contracting entity, customer terms and place of management;
  • service-performance and personnel locations;
  • permanent-establishment, agent and significant-economic-presence facts;
  • wallet, custodian and platform roles without treating them as conclusive situs;
  • gross receipts, attributable functions, assets, risks and expenses;
  • foreign tax paid and treaty relied upon; and
  • the method used to allocate a multi-jurisdictional transaction.

Withholding must be tested separately. A payment to a non-resident may fall within section 152 or another provision only if the statutory payment, payer, recipient and source conditions are satisfied. Converting the payment into a token does not avoid an otherwise applicable duty; it also does not create a withholding duty absent those elements. The proposed corrective regime should specify how an in-kind payer determines the amount, funds the withholding, reports the asset transfer and handles a transaction where no fiat is available, without imposing confiscatory over-withholding on gross transaction value.

11.4 Valuation, Basis, Timing and Records
