-| issuer sale or token generation | issuer and acquirer | issuer revenue, financing, liability, equity-like issue or customer obligation according to rights; acquisition for buyer | contract and performance terms, not mint event alone | consideration allocated to rights and obligations | issuer residence/business/source and product disclosures | token label cannot decide income recognition or ded
-| custody deposit, withdrawal or internal book transfer | customer and custodian | no customer disposal solely because custody changes if beneficial title remains; custodian earns fees | depends on legal title and service performance | customer basis continues; fee valued separately | customer subledger, omnibus wallet and safeguarding reconciliation | terms may transfer title, create a loan or p
-Gifts and succession illustrate why technical transfer and tax recognition are not synonymous. Section 75 can describe an ownership event, while section 79 can require no gain or loss and preserve character and cost in qualifying transfers, including transmission on death and specified gifts. A 2026 cost rule for inherited immovable property does not supply a corresponding virtual-asset fair-valu
-The matrix is not a schedule of new taxes. It is a discipline for applying existing law and exposing the places where Parliament, FBR or a Provincial Legislature must speak more clearly.
-## 11.3 Residence, Source and Cross-Border Activity
-Distributed infrastructure does not abolish tax residence or geographical source. The Ordinance determines residence separately for individuals, companies and associations of persons. It then brings into a resident person’s total income the Pakistan-source and foreign-source amounts within the statutory framework, while a non-resident is generally within the charge for Pakistan-source income. Tre
-For a resident business, section 101 treats business income as Pakistan-source to the extent derived from business carried on in Pakistan. For a non-resident, attribution may arise through a permanent establishment, sales through such establishment, a business connection or other specified connections. Gains on assets used in a relevant business, services, royalties, profit on debt and other cate
-Section 101’s 2024 “significant economic presence” provisions extend the business-connection enquiry to prescribed levels of transactions in goods, services or property, including downloads of data or software, and to systematic and continuous interaction through digital means with a prescribed number of users in Pakistan. The text is relevant to foreign exchanges and platforms, but it is not a l
-Certain attractive proxies are legally weak. The location of validating nodes does not necessarily identify the seller, service provider or owner. The situs of a private key says little where a cloud custodian, multisignature group or recovery provider participates. A domain name, downloadable app or Pakistani customer may support an evidential nexus, but none replaces the statutory source test.
-The minimum cross-border file should record:
-- taxpayer residence and the legal basis for it;
-- counterparty and beneficial-owner identity where required and obtainable;
-- contracting entity, customer terms and place of management;
-- service-performance and personnel locations;
-- permanent-establishment, agent and significant-economic-presence facts;
-- wallet, custodian and platform roles without treating them as conclusive situs;
-- gross receipts, attributable functions, assets, risks and expenses;
-- foreign tax paid and treaty relied upon; and
-- the method used to allocate a multi-jurisdictional transaction.
-Withholding must be tested separately. A payment to a non-resident may fall within section 152 or another provision only if the statutory payment, payer, recipient and source conditions are satisfied. Converting the payment into a token does not avoid an otherwise applicable duty; it also does not create a withholding duty absent those elements. The proposed corrective regime should specify how a
-## 11.4 Valuation, Basis, Timing and Records
-**Table 11.1 — Transaction-event tax questions requiring legislative or administrative settlement**
-| Event | Classification and taxpayer question | Timing and valuation question | Loss, source and legal vehicle |
+## 11.1 Risk and Legal Architecture
+Financial-integrity law loses accuracy when different legal states are compressed into the word “risk”. Suspicion is not guilt. A report is not a charge. A sanctions-screening match is not identity. A blockchain-analytics score is not proof. A freeze is not forfeiture. A VASP licence is not, by itself, a complete allocation of AML supervision. Each state has a different actor, legal trigger, info
+Pakistan’s starting point is nevertheless stronger than a voluntary or guidance-only model. Section 46 of the *Virtual Assets Act 2026* deems a licensed VASP to be a “financial institution” for purposes of the *Anti-Money Laundering Act 2010*. It directly requires every VASP and issuer to report suspicious transactions to the Financial Monitoring Unit (FMU), keep customer-due-diligence and transa
+The legal architecture is therefore a chain, not a single statute:
+| Layer | Controlling actor or instrument | Legal work performed | What it does not establish |
-| fiat acquisition or disposal | asset held personally, as trading stock, investment or business receipt | acquisition/disposal time; Rupee value; fees and basis | residence/source and capital/revenue character; Income Tax Ordinance or guidance within it |
-| crypto-to-crypto exchange | whether disposal and acquisition are recognised events | value of both legs at the legally selected time and source | basis carry-over or realisation; primary fiscal rule required |
-| payment for goods or services | payer disposal and recipient business receipt | value when supplied, transferred, accepted or settled | income and applicable federal/provincial sales-tax treatment |
-| mining or validation reward | operator, employee, contractor or business recipient | recognition at entitlement, receipt or disposal; network-value source | deductible electricity/equipment and source nexus; income-tax and provincial interface |
-| staking reward | ownership, delegated validation, service or investment return | accrual, receipt, claimability and disposal | slashing, locked rewards and loss treatment; fiscal rule or binding guidance |
-| airdrop or fork | recipient identity and character of unsolicited or conditional receipt | control, claimability and reliable market value | nil/allocated basis, later disposal and loss; primary or authorised administrative rule |
-| lending or liquidity provision | lender, borrower, pool participant and fee/yield character | accrual, receipt, token substitution and valuation | bad debt, impermanent loss, liquidation and cross-border source |
-| token issuance | issuer receipt, capital contribution, advance, revenue or liability | issue, vesting, performance and redemption stages | reserve deductions, refunds and issuer residence/source; primary law plus accounting alignment |
-| theft, loss or inaccessible key | beneficial owner and proof of loss | date irrecoverability becomes sufficiently established | deduction, capital loss, later recovery and evidential threshold |
-| gift, inheritance or same-owner transfer | whether beneficial ownership changed | value and basis continuity at transfer/death | anti-avoidance, succession and record rule; express legislative treatment where needed |
-Volatility is not the legal reason valuation is difficult. The deeper problem is that “price” can refer to an order-book quote, executed trade, index, oracle, thin-liquidity pool, related-party transfer, locked token, redeemable claim or manipulated market. Section 68 uses an open-market fair-market-value standard and permits the Commissioner to determine value where it is not ordinarily ascertai
-A defensible methodology should apply a hierarchy:
-1. use the actual arm’s-length transaction price on a reliable venue where it represents the rights transferred;
-2. where that price is unavailable or distorted, use a documented volume-weighted or time-consistent composite from independent liquid venues;
-3. value a redeemable claim by reference to enforceable redemption rights only after testing issuer credit, reserve access, fees, delay and restrictions;
-4. for illiquid, vested, locked or rights-bearing tokens, apply an appropriate valuation technique and disclose restrictions, assumptions and uncertainty; and
-5. where no reliable value can be established, preserve the evidence, state the uncertainty and use the statutory determination route rather than inventing precision.
-The policy must fix a consistent valuation time and time zone. A daily closing price is administratively simple but can be arbitrary for intraday exchanges. Exact transaction-time valuation is more accurate but costly for high-frequency activity. A proportionate rule can require actual executed value where available, allow a prescribed daily method for qualifying retail volumes, and require trans
-Section 71 converts foreign currency and Rupees at the State Bank rate on the relevant date; it does not classify every crypto-asset as foreign currency. A sound rule would establish fair value in reliable fiat and then translate it into Rupees at the lawful State Bank rate.
-Basis must follow units through their life. Each taxpayer should maintain, at minimum: acquisition date and time; quantity and asset identifier; chain and contract address where relevant; legal rights; wallet or account; counterparty or venue; consideration and incidental fees; valuation source; transaction identifier; beneficial owner; tax character; transfer history; and disposal proceeds. Wher
-Receipt under section 69 includes amounts actually received, applied on behalf of a person or made available. Rewards subject to a lock, slashing, unbonding period, governance condition or unresolved protocol claim require a facts-based control analysis. Recognition before the taxpayer can transfer or realise any enforceable benefit can tax an amount that never becomes available; indefinite defer
-The Ordinance generally requires taxpayer records for six years after the relevant tax year, with longer retention where proceedings remain pending. Companies have separate books-and-records duties and a ten-year retention period. VASPs should adopt the longer applicable period and preserve the raw transaction ledger, customer subledger, pricing inputs and method versions—not only a year-end stat
-## 11.5 Treatment by Actor and Function
-Tax classification should follow the actor’s function and the rights created. A single organisation may perform several functions, and each stream may have a different base.
-**Individuals and investors.** Frequency, organisation, intention, financing, holding period, use of specialised systems and relation to an existing business can inform whether activity is a business or investment, but no single factor should be treated as conclusive. A holder must separately identify acquisitions, disposals, income rewards and personal-use assertions. Wealth-statement and foreig
-**VASPs.** An exchange may earn trading commissions, spreads, listing fees, custody fees, withdrawal fees, staking commissions, data revenue and gains or losses on proprietary inventory. Customer gross trading volume is not the VASP’s income. Customer assets held without beneficial title should not be booked or taxed as the custodian’s own property merely because the custodian controls private ke
-**Brokers, dealers and market makers.** A person trading as principal may hold stock-in-trade and recognise business profits; an agent ordinarily recognises commission rather than the customer’s gross consideration. A platform acting as both principal and agent must disclose the capacity in each transaction and prevent internal pricing from shifting profit between related entities or jurisdiction
-**Issuers.** Token issuance is not one tax event. A sale can represent an immediate supply, advance consideration for future performance, a borrowing or redeemable liability, a membership or governance right, an equity-like interest, a bundled arrangement or a transfer of property. Income recognition, deductions and sales-tax treatment follow the enforceable rights and performance obligations. Tr
-**Miners and validators.** Commercial block-production or validation rewards may be business income, with ordinary-law treatment of allowable expenses. The legal recipient must be distinguished from pool operator, delegator and infrastructure host. Validator commission and delegator reward can have different character; later disposal is a separate event using the recognition value as basis.
-**Staking, lending and decentralised-finance arrangements.** Labels such as “yield”, “interest”, “liquidity mining” or “staking” do not determine character. The enquiry asks whether the taxpayer transferred title, lent property, supplied a service, entered a partnership-like arrangement, received compensation for risk, disposed of one right for another, or merely delegated validation power. Proto
-**Custodians and fiduciaries.** The tax and accounting result turns on customer title, segregation, reuse rights, insolvency treatment, restitution obligation and beneficial entitlement. If terms permit the custodian to use assets and return an equivalent, the arrangement may be economically and legally closer to a loan than a bailment or safeguarding service. If title remains with the customer,
-**Companies, funds, trusts and estates.** Entity form, tax status and governing instrument matter. A company does not receive individual personal-use treatment. A fund or trust requires identification of the taxable person, beneficiaries and distributions. On death, the legal representative must secure wallet access and preserve basis; inheritance and later disposal are separate. The VAA creates
-Actor-based rules should remain technology neutral but not evidence blind. They should require the information peculiar to virtual assets—wallets, contract rights, keys, transaction identifiers, chain events and venue pricing—only because those facts help apply the legal categories.
-## 11.6 Withholding, Reporting and Tax Administration
-A reporting system should make correct liability easier to determine; it should not substitute mass data for legal design. The existing Ordinance contains return, wealth-statement, foreign-income and foreign-asset, withholding-statement, information, record, audit and confidentiality machinery. It does not contain a complete virtual-asset reporting code.[^250]
-There is no general authority in the material inspected for a VASP to withhold tax from every virtual-asset disposal. Existing withholding sections can apply where their own conditions are met—for example, a relevant payment for goods or services or a payment to a non-resident—but a regulator should not direct a platform to deduct from gross customer proceeds without a clear charging and collecti
-Sections 165B and 165C must not be collapsed. Section 165B authorises specified information arrangements by financial institutions for automatic exchange under bilateral or multilateral instruments, with reportable-person and financial-institution terms taken from the Income Tax Rules. Section 165C requires quarterly information from online marketplaces, payment intermediaries and couriers in rel
-The domestic reporting layer should be enacted around a minimum, purpose-bound record:
-- taxpayer and controlling-person identity, residence and tax identification number;
-- licensed entity, service and account identifiers;
-- asset identifier, units and legal category used for tax treatment;
-- acquisition, disposal, transfer and reward event type;
-- fiat proceeds or fair market value, currency, valuation time and method;
-- fees, withholding where lawfully required and cost information actually held;
-- counterparty or destination category where required, distinguishing self-hosted wallets from unidentified ownership; and
-- correction, reconciliation and audit history.
-FBR should receive tax information; PVARA should receive licensing, prudential and conduct information within its mandate. Section 17 of the VAA permits information sharing with FBR, but the exchange should be governed by a published legal instrument or controlled protocol specifying fields, purposes, security, retention, onward disclosure, corrections, access logging and responsible officers. PV
-Taxpayer administration must permit correction. A customer should be able to obtain a machine-readable annual statement, challenge wrong identity or basis attribution, mark a self-transfer, supply off-platform cost evidence and receive a corrected report before assessment where practicable. FBR should publish how duplicates across VASPs, chain analytics and foreign CARF reports are reconciled. An
-Sections 174 and 176 permit records and information demands, while section 216 protects tax information subject to statutory exceptions. Those powers require audit trails, role-based access and reasoned use. Data obtained for automatic exchange should remain limited to lawful tax purposes and protected against unauthorised disclosure. Enforcement must follow assessment, notice, evidence and appea
-## 11.7 Provincial Services Tax and Federal Coordination
-Pakistan has no single national sales-tax answer for a VASP transaction. The Constitution reserves federal sales tax on goods and excludes sales tax on services from the relevant federal entry. The *Sales Tax Act 1990* charges federal sales tax on taxable supplies of goods by a registered person in the course of taxable activity and on imported goods. Its definition of goods includes movable prop
-The service leg is usually more immediate. Exchange, brokerage, dealing commission, custody, administration, advice, platform access, data, software, validation support and management may fall within one or more provincial scheduled-service categories. Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan operate distinct services-tax laws and instruments. Their schedules, descriptions, rates, exempt
-The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Act illustrates the structure without supplying a nationwide answer. It taxes services listed in its schedule, contains origin and consumption rules, can impose reverse charge for services originating outside the Province or Pakistan, values in-kind consideration by reference to open-market value, and lists categories including financial, brokerage, commission, computer/sof
-Each transaction should be disaggregated into at least:
-1. transfer of the underlying asset;
-2. exchange or brokerage commission;
-3. custody or safeguarding fee;
-4. technology, data or platform fee;
-5. advisory, management or staking commission; and
-6. any imported or intercompany service.
-Bundling does not make the components disappear. The contract and invoice should allocate consideration on an arm’s-length basis and identify the place and recipient of each service. Payment in tokens requires fair-value invoicing; it does not remove services tax.
-Coordination should be administrative rather than constitutionally assimilative. FBR and the provincial authorities can agree a common taxpayer identifier, registration-status exchange, invoice fields, audit-coordination protocol and conflict-escalation route. A lead audit may collect evidence once, but each authority must issue any demand under its own competent law. Place-of-provision conflicts
-PVARA can require a licensee to maintain jurisdictional transaction and fee data and to attest compliance. It should not decide provincial tax liability or prescribe a uniform services-tax rate. The durable settlement is a federal-provincial protocol endorsed through the appropriate intergovernmental mechanism, with published data fields and preservation of each legislature’s competence.
-## 11.8 Accounting, Audit and Financial Statements
-Tax accounting and financial reporting answer different questions. The *Companies Act 2017* requires companies to keep books and other records giving a true and fair view and covering receipts, payments, sales, purchases, assets and liabilities. Financial statements must give a true and fair view, comply with standards notified by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP), and fol
-The IFRS Interpretations Committee’s June 2019 agenda decision is important but narrow. For the cryptocurrency fact pattern it considered—a digital or virtual currency on a distributed ledger, not issued by a jurisdiction or other party and not giving rise to a contract between the holder and another party—the holding is not cash and not a financial asset. IAS 2 applies when it is held for sale i
-It does not establish that all digital tokens are IAS 38 intangibles. A tokenised share or debt instrument can create contractual or equity rights; a redeemable stablecoin can create an issuer claim; a platform balance can be a receivable; an issuer can owe future goods or services; and a custodian can hold a customer asset with a corresponding safeguarding or restitution obligation. Classificati
-The financial statements of a VASP or issuer should make the following legible:
-- proprietary assets separately from customer assets and any related safeguarding liability;
-- custody model, segregation, reuse or rehypothecation rights and insolvency exposure;
-- asset and liability classification and the reason for it;
-- valuation technique, principal market, price source, liquidity, restrictions and sensitivity;
-- revenue by principal/agent capacity and material service stream;
-- issuer redemption, reserve, performance and contingent obligations;
-- staking, lending, protocol, counterparty and concentration exposures;
-- related-party transactions, subsequent events, impairment and going-concern uncertainty; and
-- current and deferred tax positions and material uncertain tax treatments under the applicable framework.
-On-chain evidence strengthens audit but does not complete it. A signed message can support control of a key; it does not prove legal title, beneficial ownership, absence of an undisclosed obligation or completeness of all wallets. Proof of reserves can show selected assets at a point in time; without complete customer liabilities, legal ownership, encumbrances, subsequent movement and independent
-The accounting ledger should feed but not dictate the tax return. Reconciling items should identify different recognition timing, disallowed or capital expenditure, tax basis, unrealised accounting movements, withholding and services tax. A regulator should not require one “crypto accounting policy” across instruments with materially different rights.
-## 11.9 CARF, DAC8 and International Tax Transparency
-The OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) is an annual standardised automatic-exchange system for tax information. It is not a tax charge, a licensing regime or a declaration that every reported transfer is taxable. Its purpose is to give participating tax administrations consistent information about relevant crypto-asset activity that can escape conventional financial-account reporting.[^
-CARF places reporting and due-diligence duties on a Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Provider (RCASP): a person that, as a business, provides a service effectuating exchange transactions for or on behalf of customers, including by acting as counterparty or intermediary or by making available a trading platform. Jurisdictional nexus can arise through tax residence, incorporation coupled with reporti
-For reportable users and controlling persons, the standard collects identity, address, jurisdiction of residence, tax identification number and, for individuals, date of birth, subject to its detailed rules. The RCASP reports its own identity and annual aggregate information by asset type. Categories include acquisitions against fiat, disposals against fiat, exchanges for other relevant crypto-as
-That design has consequences for Pakistan. A domestic CARF law would need to define:
-- relevant crypto-assets, excluded central-bank digital currencies and specified electronic-money products, and the relationship with CRS financial assets;
-- RCASP activities and Pakistan nexus, including branches and duplicate-reporting relief;
-- reportable and excluded persons and controlling persons;
-- due-diligence, self-certification, reasonableness and change-of-circumstance duties;
-- transaction categories, valuation currency, aggregation, corrections and nil reporting;
-- record retention, audit, sanctions proportionate to culpability and a right of review;
-- confidentiality, permitted use, data-subject correction and cybersecurity controls; and
-- FBR’s authority to receive, validate, exchange and protect the information.
-PVARA should support the perimeter by giving FBR authoritative licence, service, branch and legal-person data. FBR should own tax reporting, due-diligence interpretation and international exchange. Joint rules should map PVARA’s “VASP” categories to CARF’s function-based “RCASP” test; the terms overlap but are not necessarily coextensive.
-International exchange requires more than domestic data collection. The CARF Multilateral Competent Authority Agreement (MCAA) operates on the underlying Convention or another valid exchange basis and requires notifications concerning domestic implementing law and commencement, reciprocal status, permitted use, transmission and encryption, personal-data safeguards, confidentiality and intended ex
-The OECD Global Forum’s official commitment list, last updated 23 June 2026, names 46 jurisdictions undertaking first exchanges by 2027, 29 by 2028, the United States by 2029, and five relevant jurisdictions not yet committed. Pakistan does not appear on that list. The narrow conclusion is that no Pakistan commitment is evidenced by that document as at its stated date. It does not establish rejec
-Pakistan should use a staged path:
-1. perform a legal and data-gap assessment against the CARF rules and XML schema;
-2. enact primary authority and rules only after defining scope, safeguards, sanctions and appeal;
-3. register and map RCASPs using PVARA and FBR data;
-4. run controlled test reporting with synthetic and then reconciled historical data;
-5. obtain an independent confidentiality and information-security assessment;
-6. sign or activate the relevant international instrument and make the required notifications;
-7. select exchange partners only after reciprocal legal and safeguard checks; and
-8. begin production with correction, duplicate-suppression and taxpayer access mechanisms.
-The European Union’s DAC8 is adjacent but distinct. According to the European Commission, its crypto-asset reporting rules apply from 1 January 2026, with reporting for 2026 and exchange by 30 September 2027. It covers domestic and cross-border reportable activity and can require a non-EU crypto-asset operator not authorised under MiCA to register in one Member State. DAC8 is not Pakistani law an
-Transparency must remain proportionate. A foreign report can be wrong, duplicated or based on a different residence determination. FBR should match reports to taxpayers using more than a name, notify material use where law requires, permit correction and assess tax under Pakistan’s charging provisions. CARF should close information gaps; it should not convert gross flows into presumed concealed i
-## 11.10 Public Revenue, Compliance Cost and Forecasting
-The VAA creates a lapsable PVARA Fund and identifies sources including Government grants, licence and supervision fees, fines, penalties, service charges and other receipts. It subjects the Fund to the *Public Finance Management Act 2019*, requires budgeting and accounts, and provides for Auditor-General and chartered-accountant audit and annual reporting. The public-finance statute requires self
-Three fiscal rules follow. First, licence and supervisory fees should recover the efficient cost of regulation and reflect risk or activity where law permits; they should not operate as disguised taxes. Second, penalties should deter and correct misconduct, not become a budget target that rewards enforcement volume. Third, PVARA cannot treat the gross receipts named in section 14 as an independen
-The word “lapsable” should therefore be clarified through the statute and the applicable public-finance process rather than converted into an automatic constitutional violation. The legal account must distinguish: an annual parliamentary appropriation that lapses under its own budget authority; own-source statutory receipts that must enter the Treasury Single Account or Federal Consolidated Fund
-Revenue forecasting must reject gross trading volume as a tax base. Volume includes acquisitions, self-transfers, market-making turnover, crypto-to-crypto exchanges, wash activity, losses and customer assets that are not VASP income. A defensible annual model is:
-> **Net fiscal yield = Σ[(realised taxable base by income head × effective rate) + (taxable service-fee base by province × applicable rate)] × compliance-and-collection factor − lawful credits, refunds and loss offsets − incremental administration and compliance cost.**
-The model should publish low, central and high cases for active taxpayers, realised gains and losses, business margins, fee take-rates, provincial allocation, cost-basis completeness, voluntary compliance, audit yield, bad debt, refunds and implementation cost. No Rupee forecast is credible until FBR and the Provincial Authorities can distinguish customer flow from taxable income and can reconcil
-Administrative cost includes FBR and provincial system development, data security, specialist valuation and audit capacity, dispute resolution, taxpayer support, international-exchange testing and independent assurance. Private compliance cost includes identity and residence refresh, valuation, statement correction, systems integration and retention. Rules should permit simplified valuation and a
-The fiscal dashboard should report registrations, timely and corrected reports, unmatched records, basis completeness, assessment yield net of reversals, refund delay, appeal outcomes, security incidents, cost per usable report and taxpayer-support resolution. A high volume of data or penalties is not evidence of an effective tax system.
-## 11.11 Statutory Defect and Corrective Package
-Pakistan’s current position is neither a tax vacuum nor a complete digital-asset tax regime. General federal and provincial rules can reach many receipts, gains and services. Yet the operative texts inspected do not expressly classify virtual assets, resolve the personal-use movable-property problem, prescribe a cost-basis convention, convert crypto-to-crypto and in-kind events into a consistent
-The corrective package should proceed in the following order.
-**1. Repair section 66.** Replace “Income Tax Act, 2001” with “Income Tax Ordinance, 2001” and refer, without pre-empting provincial competence, to applicable federal and provincial tax laws. State expressly that the section does not itself impose a tax, exemption or withholding obligation. Preserve FBR and Provincial Revenue Authority powers under their own enactments.
-**2. Enact a technology-neutral income-tax taxonomy.** Define “virtual asset” for tax purposes by reference to transferable digital value or rights using cryptographically secured distributed-ledger or similar technology, while coordinating exclusions for fiat currency, central-bank digital currency and instruments already governed as securities or other property. The definition should route an a
-**3. Specify events, basis and valuation.** Confirm the treatment of fiat sales, exchanges for another asset, purchases of goods or services, rewards, airdrops, forks, wrapped assets, migrations, gifts, death, loss and same-owner wallet transfers. Select a consistent cost-basis method, permit documented specific identification where administrable, address lost or inaccessible assets, and prescrib
-**4. Separate asset taxation from services tax.** FBR should issue federal guidance on the “goods” question only within the *Sales Tax Act 1990*. The Provinces should classify exchange, custody, brokerage, technology, advice and related services under their own laws. A federal-provincial protocol should supply common invoice and data fields, place-of-provision conflict handling and coordinated au
-**5. Create proportionate domestic reporting before withholding.** Require annual machine-readable statements, event and valuation fields, customer access, correction and six-year minimum records, coordinated with longer company-law retention. Do not impose blanket gross-proceeds withholding. Any withholding must identify the taxable payment, rate, credit mechanism, in-kind funding procedure, los
-**6. Build CARF through tax law.** Amend the Ordinance or enact competent primary provisions defining RCASPs, reportable persons and transactions, due diligence, valuation, records, confidentiality, sanctions and review. Authorise FBR as competent tax administrator and international exchange body; require PVARA to provide verified perimeter and licence data. Complete the MCAA, notification, infor
-**7. Align accounting and tax reconciliation.** SECP, in consultation with ICAP, FBR and PVARA, should publish rights-based application guidance rather than a universal token classification. Licensed entities should disclose customer-asset treatment, safeguarding obligations, valuation, principal/agent revenue and tax-reconciliation controls. Audit guidance should reject proof of reserves as a su
-**8. Protect public money and measure net yield.** Place fees and penalties through the PFM framework, publish cost-recovery principles, report gross and net regulatory receipts, and prohibit enforcement revenue targets. Finance Division and tax authorities should publish scenario assumptions and implementation cost before relying on digital assets in a medium-term revenue forecast.
-The sequence matters. Reporting before classification produces large but ambiguous datasets. Withholding before basis rules taxes turnover rather than income. International exchange before correction and security controls exports errors and risk. A durable fiscal regime instead begins with lawful incidence, converts rights and events into reproducible records, gives each authority only the inform
-That is the fiscal meaning of the report’s governing thesis. Code can show that value moved. Accounting can represent what an entity controls or owes. Reporting can tell a tax administration where to enquire. None can answer the constitutional question—who may impose what burden, on whom and under which law—without legislation whose authority, base and remedy remain legible.

+AMLA makes the FMU Pakistan’s financial-intelligence unit. It receives and analyses STRs and CTRs, may call for records, disseminates financial intelligence under confidentiality controls, maintains domestic and foreign linkages, and permits the Director General in the conditions of section 6(6) to order a temporary freeze for up to fifteen days. Section 6A assigns preventive supervision to the r
+The National AML/CFT Authority, established in 2023, is the policy and coordination body for strategy, action plans, legislative review, international engagement and performance. It can expose institutional gaps; it cannot merge member institutions or reallocate coercive powers by committee decision.[^217]
+Risk assessment must be dated and scoped. Pakistan’s 2023 NRA assessed VAs/VASPs as an “unregulated emerging area” only to the extent of available data and rated virtual currency as a medium terrorist-financing channel. It is not a 2026 finding that every licensed VASP, token or wallet is high risk.[^218]
+Every control must answer: **who owes it; what triggers it; what data moves to which institution; what action follows; and how error is corrected**.
+## 11.2 Reporting-Entity and VASP Coverage
+The VAA uses a direct statutory bridge for licensed VASPs. Section 46(1) says they are deemed financial institutions for AMLA purposes. That is important because AMLA’s pre-existing financial-institution definition is activity based—it includes money or value transfer, payment means, safekeeping or administration of cash or liquid securities, management of another person’s funds, financial interm
+Coverage must still be stated by legal status and activity:
+| Actor or arrangement | Financial-integrity position | Required control |
+|---|---|---|
+| PVARA-licensed VASP | deemed AMLA financial institution; direct VAA s 46 duties | full AML/CFT/CPF programme, CDD, records, monitoring, STR reporting, TFS and Travel Rule when prescribed |
+| person holding an interim NOC, sandbox admission or incubation approval | depends on the exact instrument and transition clause; not automatically identical to a final licence | verify instrument, scope, conditions, reporting-entity basis, goAML registration and transition deadline before operation |
+| issuer that is also a licensed VASP | both statuses apply; duties may overlap | one controlled programme with product-specific issuer and transfer risks, without double counting reports |
+| issuer that is not a licensed VASP | VAA s 46(2) directly names issuers, but the AMLA reporting-entity, supervisor, sanctions and protection route requires express completion | primary or valid delegated bridge identifying supervisor, FMU channel, CDD/record duties, sanctions and appeals |
+| bank, EMI, payment provider, broker or securities intermediary dealing with VAs | remains within SBP or SECP perimeter in addition to any VASP status | coordinated supervision; no lowest-standard arbitrage |
+| foreign VASP serving Pakistan | VAA territorial and licensing rules apply where the statutory nexus is met; foreign licensing does not displace Pakistan law | local permission and accountable presence or enforceable cooperation, plus counterparty due diligence |
+| pure software, self-hosted wallet user or genuinely decentralised protocol | not a VASP merely because technology facilitates transfers | control and activity test; regulate the person performing covered services, not code as if it were a legal person |

An NOC, sandbox admission or consultation application cannot silently acquire the legal effects of a licence. For each operating firm, PVARA and FMU should maintain a non-public status record showing: legal person; beneficial owners and c
+Perimeter control should be functional and anti-evasive. Splitting exchange, custody and transfer across related companies does not eliminate group risk; nor does outsourcing screening or Travel Rule messaging eliminate the licensed entity’s duty. +## 11.3 Risk Assessment and Customer Due Diligence
+AMLA requires CDD when a reporting entity enters a business relationship, conducts an occasional transaction above the prescribed threshold, encounters suspicion regardless of exemptions or thresholds, or doubts previously obtained information. It requires identity verification from reliable and independent sources, identification and reasonable verification of the beneficial owner, understanding
+For a VASP, those rules should operate across an enterprise risk assessment and a customer risk assessment. The enterprise assessment should consider at least:
+- authorised services and actual transaction patterns, not merely licence labels;
+- custody model, private-key and administrator-key concentration, smart-contract upgrade powers and reliance on third-party wallets;
+- customer types, beneficial-ownership opacity, PEP exposure, legal-person and arrangement use, nominees and cross-border groups;
+- asset characteristics, including transferability, liquidity, privacy features, governance, issuer or reserve structure, bridge and mixer exposure, without declaring a technology inherently illicit;
+- delivery channels, remote onboarding, devices, account recovery, API access, agents and introducers;
+- geographic exposure, current sanctions and FATF statements, legal interoperability and counterparty-VASP quality;
+- fiat entry and exit, bank and payment partners, cash exposure, OTC desks and mule-account indicators;
+- fraud, cyber compromise, ransomware, market abuse, tax-crime and proliferation-financing typologies that may generate predicate or associated risk; and
+- data confidence, model limitations, false-positive rates and the availability of reliable independent verification.
+The customer assessment then asks what those factors mean for the actual relationship. Standard CDD should obtain the natural person’s verified identity and contact information, expected purpose, occupation or business, source of funds where risk or product requires it, wallet and account relationships, expected volume and geography, beneficial owner and controller, and the authority of anyone ac
+Enhanced due diligence is a response to higher risk, not a euphemism for automatic refusal. Measures may include stronger identity proof, independent corporate documents, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds corroboration, senior approval, shorter review cycles, transaction limits, wallet ownership/control testing, counterparty-VASP verification, deeper reserve or issuer inquiry and enhanced moni
+Reliance and outsourcing must preserve accountability. A VASP may use an identity vendor, blockchain-analytics provider, Travel Rule network, foreign affiliate or bank information where law permits, but should know what was checked, obtain the underlying evidence without delay, test the provider, understand geographic and model limits, control subcontracting and retain a fallback. A vendor’s “ver
+FATF’s 2019 guidance supplies a useful benchmark: apply CDD to occasional VA transactions above USD/EUR 1,000, use risk-based enhanced controls rather than categorical assumptions, and coordinate Travel Rule implementation with privacy and data-protection authorities. It remains guidance, not Pakistan’s threshold rule. The VAA deliberately leaves Pakistan’s transfer trigger to PVARA; final rules
+CDD is therefore a continuing evidential process. An address check at onboarding does not control a relationship after a change in ownership, device, product, transaction pattern or sanctions exposure. VASPs should define event-driven refresh triggers as well as periodic review. A change should record its source, reviewer, effect on risk, information obtained and any monitoring consequence. They
+## 11.4 Beneficial Ownership and Control
+AMLA defines a beneficial owner as the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a customer, or on whose behalf a transaction is conducted, including a person exercising ultimate effective control over a legal person or legal arrangement. The enquiry therefore ends with a natural person unless the applicable law provides a carefully defined fallback after documented exhaustion. A company nam
+Virtual-asset systems add technical control facts that must be connected to, but not confused with, legal ownership:
+| Control fact | What it can show | What further question remains |
+|---|---|---|
+| signature from a private key | present ability to authorise a transaction | whether the signer owns the asset or acts lawfully for another |
+| custody account in a customer’s name | platform attribution and contractual account | whether the named person is the beneficial owner and whether the platform controls an omnibus wallet |
+| multisignature membership | part of the approval quorum | who selects members, changes quorum, replaces keys or directs votes |
+| smart-contract administrator or upgrade key | ability to change, pause, mint, seize or redirect the system | who ultimately controls the administrator and under what legal duty |
+| governance-token concentration | possible influence over protocol decisions | delegation, coordination, vetoes, off-chain control and whether service activity is actually performed |
+| proof-of-control message from a self-hosted wallet | control of the signing credential at that time | identity, beneficial ownership, source of assets and compromise/coercion risk |
+| transaction-graph association | technical relationship or exposure under the vendor’s model | attribution, timing, amount, model assumptions and innocent explanations |
+For licensed entities, beneficial-ownership analysis should connect four maps: legal ownership; voting and appointment rights; economic entitlement; and operational/technical control. VAA controller thresholds and licensing disclosures can identify formal controllers, but an AML enquiry should also capture acting-in-concert arrangements, side agreements, financing dependence, nominees and persons
+The same method applies to customers. For a corporate treasury using several wallets, the VASP should identify the company’s natural-person beneficial owner, the authorised officers, the persons able to sign or reset credentials, and the purpose of each wallet. For a trust or arrangement, it should identify the statutory beneficial-ownership parties and separately record who controls the relevant
+The PVARA consultation draft proposes an MLRO, enterprise risk assessment, CDD, analytics governance, transaction monitoring, Travel Rule, targeted-financial-sanctions and record-keeping controls. Those proposals are directionally useful because they link legal duties with virtual-asset operations. They are not final law and cannot repair a primary-law gap by assertion. The final instrument shoul
+False precision is a particular danger. A protocol can be influenced through a foundation, development company, validator concentration, front-end, fee switch, oracle, treasury, governance delegation, upgrade key or dominant commercial relationship. “Decentralised” is not dispositive, but neither is participation in development enough to establish control. The question is whether an identifiable
+Beneficial-ownership records must be refreshable and reconcilable. Changes in corporate registries, shareholder agreements, wallet signers, administrator keys, governance delegation or adverse information should trigger review. Where information conflicts, the VASP should resolve the inconsistency or restrict the relationship and consider reporting; it should not merely store contradictory docume
+## 11.5 Transaction Monitoring, STR/CTR and goAML
+AMLA section 7 requires a reporting entity to file an STR promptly where it knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect that a transaction or pattern involves proceeds, evades AMLA requirements, lacks an apparent lawful purpose after examination of available facts, or involves terrorist financing. All CTRs must be filed within seven working days. The 2025 reporting regulations require examination o
+The monitoring lifecycle should be auditable from event to outcome:
+| Stage | Minimum record | Decision control |
+|---|---|---|
+| data capture | customer/account, asset, chain, address, transaction hash, time, amount and valuation, fiat leg, device/API, counterparty and Travel Rule fields | completeness, clock and asset-identifier checks |
+| alert | rule/model version, factor, threshold, source data and generated time | no adverse action solely because an opaque vendor score exists |
+| triage | obvious data or list errors, duplicate alerts, customer context, exposure path and urgency | priority rules; independent sanctions route where applicable |
+| investigation | transaction pattern, beneficial owner, source/destination, off-chain records, customer explanation, prior alerts and linked accounts | proportionate information request; no tipping off |
+| disposition | reasoned close, enhanced monitoring, restriction, exit, STR, sanctions action or law-enforcement preservation | authorised reviewer and conflict control |
+| report | statutory trigger, narrative, actors, chronology, identifiers, amounts, supporting documents and urgency | submit to FMU alone through the required confidential route |
+| feedback and tuning | FMU/regulator feedback, confirmed typology, false positives and missed cases | controlled model change with validation and approval |

It may not show the natural person, authority, source of funds, reason for transfer, internal platform allocation, fiat leg or whether the transaction succeeded economically. An internal ledger can show customer attribution and net b
+A system alert is not yet statutory suspicion. The reporting entity should examine the available facts and state the reason for its disposition. It need not prove the predicate offence before reporting. Equally, it should not file defensive reports containing unanalysed transaction dumps simply because a vendor label is severe. The narrative should tell FMU what happened, why it is suspicious, wh
+CTR must remain separate. Under the 2025 regulations it is a report of a **cash transaction** at or above the threshold specified by the National Executive Committee, filed within seven working days. A VA transfer is not transformed into cash because its value exceeds a benchmark. Where an OTC transaction has a physical-cash leg, the cash report may apply; where it is purely on-chain, the relevan
+goAML is the FMU submission and data-exchange software. It is not the legal test for suspicion, a public accusation register, or automatic permission for every agency to browse customer records. The VASP forms the suspicion under law, submits the report through goAML, and protects its confidentiality. FMU analyses and disseminates under its statute. PVARA may receive supervisory information throu

Section 7(4) requires STR/CTR records for ten years, while section 7C generally requires transaction and CDD records for at least five years after the transaction or relationship. +## 11.6 Sanctions, Proliferation Financing and Asset Freezing
+“Sanctions” describes at least two different regimes. The *AML/CFT Sanctions Rules 2020* provide administrative consequences for preventive-compliance failures: monetary penalties, conditions or restrictions, licence revocation, officer disqualification, censure and remedial directions, with proportionality factors, a due-diligence defence, written notice, appeal and publication of significant sa
+Pakistan’s domestic route under the *Anti-Terrorism Act 1997* includes proscription of organisations and persons on statutory grounds and review mechanisms. Section 11O provides, upon proscription, for freezing or seizure without prior notice and without delay of money or other property owned or controlled wholly or jointly, directly or indirectly, including derived property and property of perso
+The operational decision sequence should be explicit:
+1. ingest the current official UN and domestic lists through controlled sources and record list version, publication time and ingestion time;
+2. screen customers, beneficial owners, controllers, authorised users, counterparties, addresses and relevant issuers at onboarding, list update and transaction time;
+3. treat a potential name or identifier match as an alert, resolving identity with aliases, date/place of birth, nationality, identifiers, corporate data and other reliable information;
+4. where identity is confirmed or the applicable ownership/control rule is met, act without delay under the correct legal instrument and do not wait for an STR threshold, investigation or conviction;
+5. block prohibited dealing and preserve the affected property and records without treating the property as transferred to the VASP or State;
+6. report through the instrument-specific channels, while making any independently required STR confidentially to FMU;
+7. protect non-designated customer assets, resolve false positives quickly, and provide the applicable review, delisting and expense routes; and
+8. maintain a complete decision and custody record for supervision and proceedings.
+Name screening alone is insufficient. Ownership and control can operate through companies, trusts, nominees, joint property, multisignature arrangements, custodians and persons acting on another’s direction. Conversely, a shared name, remote transaction-graph link or historical receipt from an address does not automatically prove that the current customer is designated or controlled. Both over-fr
+Proliferation financing needs an express module, not a passing reference to terrorist financing. AMLA defines proliferation financing and requires policies and procedures to implement TFS obligations; VAA section 46 requires AML/CFT/CPF controls. A VASP’s assessment should address trade and corporate opacity, dual-use procurement, front companies, sanctions evasion, maritime and logistics indicat
+Issuer and token controls are material. An FRT, ART, tokenised claim or issuer-controlled smart contract may allow minting, redemption, pausing, clawback or blacklisting. The existence of a technical function does not create authority to use it; the absence of one does not remove the legal duty to prevent dealing. Product approval should document which sanctions actions are technically possible,
+TFS effectiveness is measured by speed and accuracy together. “Without delay” is defeated by stale lists, weekend gaps, manual escalation without authority or uncertainty over token control. Legality is defeated by secret private lists, indefinite unresolved holds, failure to examine ownership, or denial of statutory expenses and review. +## 11.7 Travel Rule Legal Baseline
+The Travel Rule connects identity and transfer data that a blockchain address alone does not supply. VAA section 47 requires a licensee, for a transfer meeting or exceeding the threshold prescribed by PVARA, to obtain, hold and transmit originator and beneficiary information in a manner consistent with FATF standards. It requires compliance with applicable data-protection, data-governance and cyb
+FATF’s 2019 guidance supplies the baseline design. For a qualifying VA transfer, the ordering VASP should obtain and hold accurate required originator information and required beneficiary information and submit that information immediately and securely to the beneficiary VASP or financial institution. The beneficiary VASP should obtain and hold it. FATF used USD/EUR 1,000 as the occasional-transa
+A lawful Pakistan data path should identify each stage:
+| Stage | Actor | Minimum functional data | Control |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| pre-transfer | ordering VASP | customer/account identifier, originator name and required account/address/identity field; beneficiary name and account/address or transaction identifier; asset, chain, amount and intended counterparty VASP | CDD current; sanctions and risk screening; threshold/aggregation calculation |
+| counterparty discovery | ordering and beneficiary VASP | legal name, jurisdiction, licence/status, endpoint, security certificate and message capability | counterparty due diligence; no reliance on a network label alone |
+| transmission | ordering VASP | required originator/beneficiary message linked unambiguously to the transfer | immediate, secure, encrypted, authenticated and integrity-protected channel |
+| receipt | beneficiary VASP | message receipt, match to pending transfer and missing/invalid-field status | accept, hold, reject, return or escalate under prescribed risk-based rules |
+| execution | relevant VASP(s) | transaction hash or internal transfer reference, time, amount and disposition | Travel Rule data need not be on-chain but must remain reliably linked |
+| post-transfer | each VASP | full message, changes, exceptions, communications and monitoring disposition | retention, access restriction, audit log, STR/TFS route and lawful disclosure |
+The originator data set should distinguish name; account number or unique transaction identifier; and the additional identity field or fields required by the adopted standard, such as address, national identity or customer identification number, or date and place of birth. The beneficiary set should include name and account number, wallet address or other unique transaction identifier. A final Pa
+Travel Rule data should move separately but synchronously with the value-transfer instruction. Putting personal information in calldata, a token memo or another permanent public field can make it globally visible, immutable and difficult to correct. A secure off-chain messaging protocol, direct bilateral channel or other mechanism can comply if it authenticates the parties, protects confidentiali
+Accordingly, keeping personally identifiable information off-chain should be the privacy-by-design default for regulatory standards and system architecture unless a defined lawful purpose, necessity assessment and technical safeguard justify another treatment. That is a recommended design standard, not a statement that present Pakistani law imposes an absolute prohibition on every on-chain person
+Counterparty-VASP due diligence is distinct from customer CDD. Before relying on another provider, a licensee should verify the provider’s legal identity, relevant jurisdiction and permission, physical or accountable presence, AML supervisor, ownership/control, sanctions exposure, Travel Rule capability, security, data location, breach history, response route and treatment of missing information.
+Missing or late data requires controlled choices. Final rules should prohibit a mechanical universal answer—always execute, always reject, or always freeze—because the legal consequence depends on amount, suspicion, sanctions, customer risk, reason for failure, counterparty quality and whether the message can be cured. The beneficiary VASP should be able to hold a transfer in a segregated pending
+Data protection is part of compliance, not an exception to it. VAA section 49 limits collection, use and sharing to necessary or lawful purposes and requires informed consent for non-essential processing. Travel Rule processing should instead be anchored in the statutory obligation, necessity and the applicable lawful-transfer basis; consent should not be presented as freely optional where refusa
+FATF’s 2025 targeted update found that implementation and enforcement of the Travel Rule remained incomplete across jurisdictions. That fact counsels a managed interoperability period, not postponement of Pakistan’s rule. PVARA should publish conformance tests, message examples, counterparty-failure handling and a staged transition, while retaining direct supervisory access to evidence of complia
+## 11.8 Threshold Precision and Cross-Border Interoperability
+There is no universal domestic Travel Rule threshold. FATF’s benchmark is USD/EUR 1,000. United States funds-transfer rules, as explained by FinCEN, generally apply the funds Travel Rule to transmittals of funds of USD 3,000 or more and require specified transmittor and recipient information. Other jurisdictions use their own legislation, including zero-threshold or different data approaches. The
+VAA section 47 assigns Pakistan’s threshold to PVARA. Draft regulation 100 proposes, pending prescription, the PKR equivalent of USD/EUR 1,000. Because PVARA’s official page states that the draft is not final and is subject to revision, that proposal cannot be represented as the operative domestic number. The final instrument should identify its parent power and publication/effective date and spe
+- the number and currency or benchmark, including whether different data obligations apply above and below it;
+- the authoritative conversion source, valuation timestamp, treatment of spreads and unavailable/stale prices;
+- asset identification, including wrapped assets, stable-value assets, illiquid tokens and transfers with several assets;
+- aggregation of linked transfers by customer, beneficiary, counterparty, device, address and time window;
+- anti-structuring treatment, while preserving the independent suspicion test at every amount;
+- which event measures the threshold—order, acceptance, broadcast, confirmation, settlement or credit;
+- treatment of internal ledger transfers, failed transactions, fee-only transfers, refunds, returns, batching, UTXO change and smart-contract interactions;
+- responsibilities where more than one VASP participates, or where a bank or payment provider controls a fiat leg;
+- rules for unavailable or conflicting counterparty requirements; and
+- change control, notice, grandfathering and machine-readable publication.
+Thresholds ration a minimum data duty; they do not create a safe harbour. A transfer below the number remains subject to sanctions, suspicion, CDD where otherwise triggered, monitoring and any verified customer data requirement. A transfer above it does not become suspicious by amount alone. The system should record both the threshold decision and the independent risk decision.
+Cross-border interoperability also requires a conflict rule. The ordering VASP may face Pakistan’s minimum fields, a beneficiary jurisdiction’s additional fields, privacy or localisation restrictions and a counterparty protocol’s technical requirements. The final rules should permit additional necessary fields where lawfully required, but require the VASP to identify the legal basis, minimise dat
+FATF revised Recommendation 16 in June 2025 and stated that the changes should apply by the end of 2030. Pakistan’s present rule should therefore be standards-aware but legally time-correct: implement the current VAA and applicable FATF baseline now, design fields and systems that can migrate, and amend the domestic instrument through lawful process when the revised international requirements bec
+The transition should use a published “sunrise” sequence: final rule and schema; provider registration; test environment; bilateral and network conformance; production for high-capability corridors; monitored exception period; full enforcement; and periodic review. Each stage should identify what duty applies, what evidence PVARA will inspect and what happens when a foreign provider cannot receiv
+## 11.9 Self-Hosted Wallets, DeFi and Control Tests
+A transfer involving a self-hosted or unhosted wallet has only one regulated VASP endpoint. It does not have no identifiable actor: the VASP still knows its customer and can collect the intended counterparty, purpose, wallet, asset and transaction information. It also does not automatically have a second VASP capable of receiving a Travel Rule message. Final rules should recognise that difference
+Risk-based controls can include obtaining the counterparty’s name and wallet address, checking sanctions and transaction exposure, asking the customer about purpose and relationship, testing wallet control where proportionate, applying limits or enhanced review, and monitoring the completed transaction. A cryptographic signature, micro-transaction or other proof can show control of a wallet crede
+Restrictions require evidence and a source. A privacy-enhancing asset, mixer exposure, bridge, peer-to-peer transfer or self-hosted wallet may increase opacity or complicate counterparty verification in particular facts. None is inherently proof of laundering. The VASP should record the exposure path, timing, value, service attribution, model confidence, customer explanation and other facts. It m
+“DeFi” similarly describes architecture, not a legal exemption or legal person. FATF’s functional approach asks whether creators, owners, operators or other persons retain control or sufficient influence and perform VASP functions, even where software presents itself as decentralised. The analysis should test:
+| Control surface | Evidence to examine | Regulatory significance |
+|---|---|---|
+| upgrade, pause, mint, seize or parameter keys | key holders, replacement power, multisig quorum and actual use | ability to control core service or customer exposure |
+| front-end and API | operator, geoblocking, fees, order routing and custody connections | performance or facilitation of covered service for users |
+| treasury and fee switch | beneficial recipients, discretionary allocation and revenue dependence | economic control and service business evidence |
+| governance | token concentration, delegation, veto, quorum, off-chain agreements and emergency councils | effective influence, not merely formal voting percentages |
+| oracle, bridge and validator dependencies | selection, replacement, concentration and contractual control | operational control and third-party risk |
+| development and brand | company/foundation role, employment, repositories, marketing and user commitments | relevant context but not alone conclusive |
+The conclusion must identify a person and covered activity. Code cannot file an STR, appoint an MLRO, receive notice or exercise an appeal. If no person performs or controls the regulated service on the evidence, calling the protocol a VASP does not solve supervision. If an identifiable person does, “decentralised” branding does not remove the duty.[^240]
+VASP interaction with DeFi should still be controlled where no DeFi operator is regulated. Product approval should evaluate contract risk, administrator powers, sanctions and illicit-finance exposure, oracle and bridge dependencies, liquidity, transaction finality, customer disclosure, monitoring coverage, custody consequences and incident response. The control is placed on the licensed entity’s
+## 11.10 Investigations, Seizure and Evidentiary Custody
+Financial-integrity systems generate leads and preserve records; they do not confer every investigative power on PVARA, FMU or a VASP. VAA sections 50–61 create offences, investigation and enforcement mechanisms, administrative sanctions, emergency intervention and blocking powers. AMLA gives FMU information and temporary-freeze functions and assigns investigation/prosecution to authorised agenci
+For a digital asset, preservation has two objects: evidence and value. Moving value to a secure wallet may protect it from dissipation but creates a new transaction, fees, tax/accounting questions, key risk and possible contamination of the evidential narrative.
