Chapter 11 — Financial Integrity: AML/CFT, Sanctions and Travel Rule

Chapter status: SUBSTANTIVE WORKING DRAFT — AUTHOR REVIEW AND FINAL CITATION CLEARANCE PENDING

Evidence cut-off for this chapter: 16 August 2026

11.1 Risk and Legal Architecture

Financial-integrity law loses accuracy when different legal states are compressed into the word “risk”. Suspicion is not guilt. A report is not a charge. A sanctions-screening match is not identity. A blockchain-analytics score is not proof. A freeze is not forfeiture. A VASP licence is not, by itself, a complete allocation of AML supervision. Each state has a different actor, legal trigger, information set, consequence and route of review.

Pakistan’s starting point is nevertheless stronger than a voluntary or guidance-only model. Section 46 of the Virtual Assets Act 2026 deems a licensed VASP to be a “financial institution” for purposes of the Anti-Money Laundering Act 2010. It directly requires every VASP and issuer to report suspicious transactions to the Financial Monitoring Unit (FMU), keep customer-due-diligence and transaction records, and maintain internal AML/CFT and counter-proliferation-financing controls under a designated officer. Section 47 creates a Travel Rule duty at the threshold to be prescribed by PVARA. Sections 48 and 49 add secure reporting interfaces and limits on non-essential processing.215

The legal architecture is therefore a chain, not a single statute:

LayerControlling actor or instrumentLegal work performedWhat it does not establish
primary VASP bridgeParliament, VAA ss 46–49reporting-entity treatment, direct duties, Travel Rule baseline, reporting/data controlsfinal threshold, data schema or proof of PVARA’s AMLA Schedule IV designation
general preventive lawAMLA and instruments under itFMU, reporting, CDD, beneficial ownership, records, TFS policies and compliance sanctionsactivity-specific custody or virtual-asset technical design
AML supervisionSchedule IV regulatory authorities and oversight bodiesrule-making, inspection, information, sanctions and TFS supervision within assigned perimetercriminal guilt or universal jurisdiction over tokenised products
national coordinationNational AML/CFT Authoritynational strategy, action plans, cross-government coordination, international focal-point and performance reviewoperational receipt of every STR or replacement of sector regulators and investigators
targeted financial sanctionsUN implementation instruments and ATA domestic proscription routedesignation-based prohibition, freeze/seizure and related reportingan ordinary risk score or suspicion-based determination
investigation and adjudicationFMU dissemination, authorised agencies, prosecutors and courts under source-specific lawpreservation, production, search, seizure, proof, trial and forfeitureretrospective validation of an unlawful private or public intervention
international benchmarkFATF Recommendations and guidancecommon outcomes, interoperability and effectiveness testsself-executing Pakistani law or a universal domestic threshold

AMLA makes the FMU Pakistan’s financial-intelligence unit. It receives and analyses STRs and CTRs, may call for records, disseminates financial intelligence under confidentiality controls, maintains domestic and foreign linkages, and permits the Director General in the conditions of section 6(6) to order a temporary freeze for up to fifteen days. Section 6A assigns preventive supervision to the regulators and self-regulatory oversight bodies listed in Schedule IV. The distinction is foundational: FMU owns the intelligence-reporting channel; the assigned regulator owns compliance supervision; an investigator exercises powers under its enabling law; a court determines matters allocated to it.216

The National AML/CFT Authority, established in 2023, is the policy and coordination body for strategy, action plans, legislative review, international engagement and performance. It can expose institutional gaps; it cannot merge member institutions or reallocate coercive powers by committee decision.217

Risk assessment must be dated and scoped. Pakistan’s 2023 NRA assessed VAs/VASPs as an “unregulated emerging area” only to the extent of available data and rated virtual currency as a medium terrorist-financing channel. It is not a 2026 finding that every licensed VASP, token or wallet is high risk.218

Every control must answer: who owes it; what triggers it; what data moves to which institution; what action follows; and how error is corrected.

11.2 Reporting-Entity and VASP Coverage

The VAA uses a direct statutory bridge for licensed VASPs. Section 46(1) says they are deemed financial institutions for AMLA purposes. That is important because AMLA’s pre-existing financial-institution definition is activity based—it includes money or value transfer, payment means, safekeeping or administration of cash or liquid securities, management of another person’s funds, financial intermediation and related activities—but was not written as a complete virtual-asset taxonomy. Deeming avoids requiring every licensed exchange, broker, transfer provider or custodian to be forced analogically into a legacy category before core AML duties attach.219

Coverage must still be stated by legal status and activity:

Actor or arrangementFinancial-integrity positionRequired control
PVARA-licensed VASPdeemed AMLA financial institution; direct VAA s 46 dutiesfull AML/CFT/CPF programme, CDD, records, monitoring, STR reporting, TFS and Travel Rule when prescribed
person holding an interim NOC, sandbox admission or incubation approvaldepends on the exact instrument and transition clause; not automatically identical to a final licenceverify instrument, scope, conditions, reporting-entity basis, goAML registration and transition deadline before operation
issuer that is also a licensed VASPboth statuses apply; duties may overlapone controlled programme with product-specific issuer and transfer risks, without double counting reports
issuer that is not a licensed VASPVAA s 46(2) directly names issuers, but the AMLA reporting-entity, supervisor, sanctions and protection route requires express completionprimary or valid delegated bridge identifying supervisor, FMU channel, CDD/record duties, sanctions and appeals
bank, EMI, payment provider, broker or securities intermediary dealing with VAsremains within SBP or SECP perimeter in addition to any VASP statuscoordinated supervision; no lowest-standard arbitrage
foreign VASP serving PakistanVAA territorial and licensing rules apply where the statutory nexus is met; foreign licensing does not displace Pakistan lawlocal permission and accountable presence or enforceable cooperation, plus counterparty due diligence
pure software, self-hosted wallet user or genuinely decentralised protocolnot a VASP merely because technology facilitates transferscontrol and activity test; regulate the person performing covered services, not code as if it were a legal person

The issuer sentence exposes a real plumbing problem. Section 46(2) directly orders every “Virtual Asset Service Provider and Issuer” to report STRs, retain records and maintain controls. But AMLA defines a reporting entity as a financial institution, DNFBP or other notified person, while VAA section 46(1) deems only licensed VASPs—not every issuer—to be a financial institution. If a non-VASP issuer is not otherwise a reporting entity, legislation must still identify how AMLA protections, FMU reporting, CDD triggers, supervisory inspection, administrative sanctions and appeal attach. An obligation should not be announced without the institution capable of supervising it.

The status the Act confers must also be stated precisely, because an earlier and still-circulating account of Pakistan's position is wrong for the law in force. On that account, the transitional framework treated VASPs as designated non-financial businesses and professions (DNFBPs), and the 2026 Act "elevated" them to financial institutions. Whatever the position under the lapsed Virtual Assets Ordinance 2025, the enacted text settles the present question in one direction only: section 46(1) deems licensed VASPs to be financial institutions, and the expressions "designated non-financial business and profession" and "DNFBP" do not appear anywhere in the Act. Section 74 preserves things validly done under the Ordinance, but it preserves acts, not a superseded classification. The distinction is not terminological. Financial-institution status engages AMLA's customer-due-diligence, record-keeping and reporting suite directly; DNFBP status would have engaged a different supervisory route through FBR and the self-regulatory bodies listed in Schedule IV. A chapter that described VASPs as DNFBPs would misstate both the obligation set and the supervisor. The Ordinance's own text could not be read for this chapter: the copy on the official Pakistan Code site is a scanned image without machine-readable text, and no other official version was located. Any historical claim about the Ordinance's treatment of VASPs is therefore recorded as unverified pending acquisition of a legible official copy.220

There is a related regulator-allocation problem, and it is more acute than a missing notification. The official AMLA consolidation inspected for this chapter lists SBP, SECP, FBR, the National Savings supervisory board, the Pakistan Post supervisory board and — at item 1(vi) — "any other such entity or regulatory authority as may be notified by the Federal Government". That consolidation is updated to 2 September 2022 and therefore predates PVARA, so it cannot evidence the post-PVARA position either way. The decisive point lies in the 2026 Act itself: the expressions "Schedule IV" and "section 6A" appear nowhere in it. Section 46(3) orders PVARA to align its supervisory framework through AML/CFT/CPF Regulations, but aligning a framework with FATF standards is not the same legislative act as designating an AML/CFT regulatory authority under section 6A(1). Parliament used the deeming route for the regulated persons and left the regulator designation untouched. Searches of PVARA's own instrument register, the Pakistan Code and general official sources located no Gazette notification under item 1(vi) completing that step. The responsible conclusion is not that no notification can exist; it is that the material located does not prove the allocation, and that the Act did not perform it. The Government should publish the operative instrument if it exists, and notify PVARA under item 1(vi) or amend Schedule IV if it does not.221

Transitional labels require equal discipline. PVARA's official consultation page says the 2026 VASP Regulations are a draft, not final, and subject to revision; the consultation itself ran from 11 June to 2 July 2026 and has closed, and PVARA's regulations register still lists only the Act, the No Objection Certificate Regulations and the Incubation Guidelines for the Regulatory Sandbox. The window for comment has therefore shut without the instrument issuing, which converts an ordinary drafting interval into a measurable completion failure. An NOC, sandbox admission or consultation application cannot silently acquire the legal effects of a licence. For each operating firm, PVARA and FMU should maintain a non-public status record showing: legal person; beneficial owners and controllers; permission type; authorised services; effective and expiry dates; conditions; assigned AML supervisor; MLRO; goAML organisation identifier; bank relationship; foreign permissions; and transition date. A public register should disclose the permission type and scope without exposing sensitive reporting data.222

Perimeter control should be functional and anti-evasive. Splitting exchange, custody and transfer across related companies does not eliminate group risk; nor does outsourcing screening or Travel Rule messaging eliminate the licensed entity’s duty. Conversely, incidental software development, non-custodial interface provision or protocol publication should not be declared regulated activity without the statutory service and control facts. The same evidence must support both inclusion and exclusion.

11.3 Risk Assessment and Customer Due Diligence

AMLA requires CDD when a reporting entity enters a business relationship, conducts an occasional transaction above the prescribed threshold, encounters suspicion regardless of exemptions or thresholds, or doubts previously obtained information. It requires identity verification from reliable and independent sources, identification and reasonable verification of the beneficial owner, understanding of purpose and intended nature, and ongoing monitoring. Failure to complete required CDD means the entity should not open or perform the transaction, or should terminate the relationship, and should consider an STR. Anonymous or fictitious relationships are prohibited.223

For a VASP, those rules should operate across an enterprise risk assessment and a customer risk assessment. The enterprise assessment should consider at least:

  • authorised services and actual transaction patterns, not merely licence labels;
  • custody model, private-key and administrator-key concentration, smart-contract upgrade powers and reliance on third-party wallets;
  • customer types, beneficial-ownership opacity, PEP exposure, legal-person and arrangement use, nominees and cross-border groups;
  • asset characteristics, including transferability, liquidity, privacy features, governance, issuer or reserve structure, bridge and mixer exposure, without declaring a technology inherently illicit;
  • delivery channels, remote onboarding, devices, account recovery, API access, agents and introducers;
  • geographic exposure, current sanctions and FATF statements, legal interoperability and counterparty-VASP quality;
  • fiat entry and exit, bank and payment partners, cash exposure, OTC desks and mule-account indicators;
  • fraud, cyber compromise, ransomware, market abuse, tax-crime and proliferation-financing typologies that may generate predicate or associated risk; and
  • data confidence, model limitations, false-positive rates and the availability of reliable independent verification.

The customer assessment then asks what those factors mean for the actual relationship. Standard CDD should obtain the natural person’s verified identity and contact information, expected purpose, occupation or business, source of funds where risk or product requires it, wallet and account relationships, expected volume and geography, beneficial owner and controller, and the authority of anyone acting for another. Legal persons require constitutive and registry information, registered and operating address, directors or equivalent officers, ownership chain, natural-person beneficial owner, purpose, expected counterparties and evidence of authority. Legal arrangements require the settlor, trustee, protector where any, beneficiaries or class, other effective controller and the person providing assets.

Enhanced due diligence is a response to higher risk, not a euphemism for automatic refusal. Measures may include stronger identity proof, independent corporate documents, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds corroboration, senior approval, shorter review cycles, transaction limits, wallet ownership/control testing, counterparty-VASP verification, deeper reserve or issuer inquiry and enhanced monitoring. A politically exposed person is a risk-management category requiring source and approval measures under the applicable framework; it is not an allegation of crime.

Reliance and outsourcing must preserve accountability. A VASP may use an identity vendor, blockchain-analytics provider, Travel Rule network, foreign affiliate or bank information where law permits, but should know what was checked, obtain the underlying evidence without delay, test the provider, understand geographic and model limits, control subcontracting and retain a fallback. A vendor’s “verified” flag is not a legal conclusion when the vendor never checked the beneficial owner or the customer’s authority over a wallet.

FATF’s 2019 guidance supplies a useful benchmark: apply CDD to occasional VA transactions above USD/EUR 1,000, use risk-based enhanced controls rather than categorical assumptions, and coordinate Travel Rule implementation with privacy and data-protection authorities. It remains guidance, not Pakistan’s threshold rule. The VAA deliberately leaves Pakistan’s transfer trigger to PVARA; final rules must perform that legislative task in a manner consistent with AMLA and the parent Act.224

CDD is therefore a continuing evidential process. An address check at onboarding does not control a relationship after a change in ownership, device, product, transaction pattern or sanctions exposure. VASPs should define event-driven refresh triggers as well as periodic review. A change should record its source, reviewer, effect on risk, information obtained and any monitoring consequence. They should also record why a control was proportionate: excessive data collection creates privacy, security and exclusion risk without necessarily improving detection.

11.4 Beneficial Ownership and Control

AMLA defines a beneficial owner as the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a customer, or on whose behalf a transaction is conducted, including a person exercising ultimate effective control over a legal person or legal arrangement. The enquiry therefore ends with a natural person unless the applicable law provides a carefully defined fallback after documented exhaustion. A company name, nominee shareholder, trust label, exchange account or wallet address is a starting point, not the answer.225

Virtual-asset systems add technical control facts that must be connected to, but not confused with, legal ownership:

Control factWhat it can showWhat further question remains
signature from a private keypresent ability to authorise a transactionwhether the signer owns the asset or acts lawfully for another
custody account in a customer’s nameplatform attribution and contractual accountwhether the named person is the beneficial owner and whether the platform controls an omnibus wallet
multisignature membershippart of the approval quorumwho selects members, changes quorum, replaces keys or directs votes
smart-contract administrator or upgrade keyability to change, pause, mint, seize or redirect the systemwho ultimately controls the administrator and under what legal duty
governance-token concentrationpossible influence over protocol decisionsdelegation, coordination, vetoes, off-chain control and whether service activity is actually performed
proof-of-control message from a self-hosted walletcontrol of the signing credential at that timeidentity, beneficial ownership, source of assets and compromise/coercion risk
transaction-graph associationtechnical relationship or exposure under the vendor’s modelattribution, timing, amount, model assumptions and innocent explanations

For licensed entities, beneficial-ownership analysis should connect four maps: legal ownership; voting and appointment rights; economic entitlement; and operational/technical control. VAA controller thresholds and licensing disclosures can identify formal controllers, but an AML enquiry should also capture acting-in-concert arrangements, side agreements, financing dependence, nominees and persons with decisive negative rights. A percentage is a rule for identifying mandatory cases, not permission to ignore effective control below it.

The same method applies to customers. For a corporate treasury using several wallets, the VASP should identify the company’s natural-person beneficial owner, the authorised officers, the persons able to sign or reset credentials, and the purpose of each wallet. For a trust or arrangement, it should identify the statutory beneficial-ownership parties and separately record who controls the relevant keys. For an agent or broker, it must determine whether the broker is the customer, acts for disclosed principals, or is improperly shielding them.

The PVARA consultation draft proposes an MLRO, enterprise risk assessment, CDD, analytics governance, transaction monitoring, Travel Rule, targeted-financial-sanctions and record-keeping controls. Those proposals are directionally useful because they link legal duties with virtual-asset operations. They are not final law and cannot repair a primary-law gap by assertion. The final instrument should use the AMLA definition, state how control tests interact with VAA controller disclosure, and prevent a technical proof-of-wallet procedure from being sold as beneficial-ownership verification.226

False precision is a particular danger. A protocol can be influenced through a foundation, development company, validator concentration, front-end, fee switch, oracle, treasury, governance delegation, upgrade key or dominant commercial relationship. “Decentralised” is not dispositive, but neither is participation in development enough to establish control. The question is whether an identifiable person performs or controls a covered service for or on behalf of another and can change, restrict, profit from or direct material operations. The evidence and reasoning should be recorded for both a decision to regulate and a decision not to regulate.

Beneficial-ownership records must be refreshable and reconcilable. Changes in corporate registries, shareholder agreements, wallet signers, administrator keys, governance delegation or adverse information should trigger review. Where information conflicts, the VASP should resolve the inconsistency or restrict the relationship and consider reporting; it should not merely store contradictory documents and call the file complete.

11.5 Transaction Monitoring, STR/CTR and goAML

AMLA section 7 requires a reporting entity to file an STR promptly where it knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect that a transaction or pattern involves proceeds, evades AMLA requirements, lacks an apparent lawful purpose after examination of available facts, or involves terrorist financing. All CTRs must be filed within seven working days. The 2025 reporting regulations require examination of available facts, risk-based alerts and red flags, prompt STR submission through goAML in the form required by FMU, and immediate written notice to the Director General where a potential temporary freeze under section 6(6) is required.227

The monitoring lifecycle should be auditable from event to outcome:

StageMinimum recordDecision control
data capturecustomer/account, asset, chain, address, transaction hash, time, amount and valuation, fiat leg, device/API, counterparty and Travel Rule fieldscompleteness, clock and asset-identifier checks
alertrule/model version, factor, threshold, source data and generated timeno adverse action solely because an opaque vendor score exists
triageobvious data or list errors, duplicate alerts, customer context, exposure path and urgencypriority rules; independent sanctions route where applicable
investigationtransaction pattern, beneficial owner, source/destination, off-chain records, customer explanation, prior alerts and linked accountsproportionate information request; no tipping off
dispositionreasoned close, enhanced monitoring, restriction, exit, STR, sanctions action or law-enforcement preservationauthorised reviewer and conflict control
reportstatutory trigger, narrative, actors, chronology, identifiers, amounts, supporting documents and urgencysubmit to FMU alone through the required confidential route
feedback and tuningFMU/regulator feedback, confirmed typology, false positives and missed casescontrolled model change with validation and approval

On-chain and off-chain information must be joined. A public ledger can show that an address sent a quantity of a token to another address at a time and block height. It may not show the natural person, authority, source of funds, reason for transfer, internal platform allocation, fiat leg or whether the transaction succeeded economically. An internal ledger can show customer attribution and net balance while omitting the external path. Effective monitoring reconciles both and preserves the uncertainty.

A system alert is not yet statutory suspicion. The reporting entity should examine the available facts and state the reason for its disposition. It need not prove the predicate offence before reporting. Equally, it should not file defensive reports containing unanalysed transaction dumps simply because a vendor label is severe. The narrative should tell FMU what happened, why it is suspicious, who may be involved, which identifiers and counterparties matter, what action the VASP took, and what information remains uncertain.

CTR must remain separate. Under the 2025 regulations it is a report of a cash transaction at or above the threshold specified by the National Executive Committee, filed within seven working days. A VA transfer is not transformed into cash because its value exceeds a benchmark. Where an OTC transaction has a physical-cash leg, the cash report may apply; where it is purely on-chain, the relevant routes are monitoring, STR and Travel Rule. Structuring below a threshold may itself contribute to suspicion, but does not justify rewriting the CTR definition.228

goAML is the FMU submission and data-exchange software. It is not the legal test for suspicion, a public accusation register, or automatic permission for every agency to browse customer records. The VASP forms the suspicion under law, submits the report through goAML, and protects its confidentiality. FMU analyses and disseminates under its statute. PVARA may receive supervisory information through a separately lawful route, but STR content and access should follow the AMLA allocation rather than a general “real-time access” label.229

Confidentiality and retention require category mapping. AMLA protects STR/CTR secrecy and prohibits tipping off; the reporting regulations require assistance to remain confidential. Section 7(4) requires STR/CTR records for ten years, while section 7C generally requires transaction and CDD records for at least five years after the transaction or relationship. VAA section 47 requires Travel Rule and CDD records for no less than the AMLA period. A compliant schedule should therefore identify record category, start event, minimum period, legal hold, access, encryption, deletion and cross-border location. “Keep everything forever” is neither a retention rule nor a security policy.

11.6 Sanctions, Proliferation Financing and Asset Freezing

“Sanctions” describes at least two different regimes. The AML/CFT Sanctions Rules 2020 provide administrative consequences for preventive-compliance failures: monetary penalties, conditions or restrictions, licence revocation, officer disqualification, censure and remedial directions, with proportionality factors, a due-diligence defence, written notice, appeal and publication of significant sanctions. Targeted financial sanctions (TFS), by contrast, implement designation-based prohibitions and freezing duties under UN and domestic counter-terrorism law. A compliance penalty after breach is not the same event as freezing designated property without delay.230

Pakistan’s domestic route under the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997 includes proscription of organisations and persons on statutory grounds and review mechanisms. Section 11O provides, upon proscription, for freezing or seizure without prior notice and without delay of money or other property owned or controlled wholly or jointly, directly or indirectly, including derived property and property of persons acting on behalf or at the direction of the proscribed person. Action must be reported within forty-eight hours; the Government must inquire into ownership and control and immediately release wrongly frozen or seized property. Sections 11OO and following provide access to basic or extraordinary expenses, legal fees and judicial attachment or forfeiture routes.231

Two features of that architecture are routinely misdescribed, and both matter operationally. The first is the split between the two designation routes. The United Nations route is grounded in section 2 of the United Nations (Security Council) Act 1948 and the Federal Government’s implementing order, S.R.O. 261(I)/2019 of 4 March 2019 — the UNSC (Freezing and Seizure) Order 2019 — and is organised by UN committee: the Al-Qaida/Da'esh committee and the Taliban committee, whose listings descend from resolutions 1267 (1999), 1333 (2000), 1988 (2011), 1989 (2011), 2253 (2015) and 2368 (2017). Resolution 1373 does not travel by that route. It has no standing list, because it obliges states to designate for themselves; Pakistan discharges it domestically through the proscription and freezing provisions of the ATA — sections 11B, 11E, 11EE, 11EEEEE, 11O, 11OO and 11P. A screening system that files 1373 alongside 1267 in a single “UN list” ingestion pipeline will look compliant and be wrong: it will wait for a list that is never published, and miss the domestic Schedule that actually carries the obligation.232

The second is the identity of the designating authority. Organisations are proscribed by the Ministry of Interior under section 11B(1) read with the First Schedule; persons are placed on the Fourth Schedule by notification of the provincial Home Department. NACTA publishes, standardises and reconciles those lists and supports implementation, but it is not the proscribing authority and states so expressly. A VASP that treats a NACTA web page as the legal instrument, rather than as the published record of instruments made elsewhere, has misidentified both the source of its freezing duty and the body to which representations should be directed.233

It should also be said plainly, against a common overstatement, that the ATA freeze is not a power exercised beyond review. It is deliberately ex parte and immediate — that is its point, and prior notice would defeat it — but section 11O(4) requires the Federal Government, on the application of any affected person, to inquire into ownership and control and to order immediate release where property has wrongly been frozen or seized; section 11OO preserves access to basic and extraordinary expenses and legal fees; and sections 11P to 11S route attachment, forfeiture and appeal through the courts. Speed at the point of action and review after it are not in tension. Describing the regime as one that “bypasses judicial or administrative review” both misstates the statute and, more practically, conceals from a wrongly frozen customer the remedy the Act in fact provides.234

The operational decision sequence should be explicit:

1. ingest the current official UN and domestic lists through controlled sources and record list version, publication time and ingestion time;

2. screen customers, beneficial owners, controllers, authorised users, counterparties, addresses and relevant issuers at onboarding, list update and transaction time;

3. treat a potential name or identifier match as an alert, resolving identity with aliases, date/place of birth, nationality, identifiers, corporate data and other reliable information;

4. where identity is confirmed or the applicable ownership/control rule is met, act without delay under the correct legal instrument and do not wait for an STR threshold, investigation or conviction;

5. block prohibited dealing and preserve the affected property and records without treating the property as transferred to the VASP or State;

6. report through the instrument-specific channels, while making any independently required STR confidentially to FMU;

7. protect non-designated customer assets, resolve false positives quickly, and provide the applicable review, delisting and expense routes; and

8. maintain a complete decision and custody record for supervision and proceedings.

Name screening alone is insufficient. Ownership and control can operate through companies, trusts, nominees, joint property, multisignature arrangements, custodians and persons acting on another’s direction. Conversely, a shared name, remote transaction-graph link or historical receipt from an address does not automatically prove that the current customer is designated or controlled. Both over-freezing and under-freezing are control failures.

Proliferation financing needs an express module, not a passing reference to terrorist financing. AMLA defines proliferation financing and requires policies and procedures to implement TFS obligations; VAA section 46 requires AML/CFT/CPF controls. A VASP’s assessment should address trade and corporate opacity, dual-use procurement, front companies, sanctions evasion, maritime and logistics indicators where relevant, state-linked or controlled counterparties, stable-value settlement, rapid layering, chain hopping and use of intermediaries. The entity should not attempt to adjudicate geopolitical guilt. It should apply current legal designations, identify suspicious financial behaviour, preserve evidence and report through the correct route.235

Issuer and token controls are material. An FRT, ART, tokenised claim or issuer-controlled smart contract may allow minting, redemption, pausing, clawback or blacklisting. The existence of a technical function does not create authority to use it; the absence of one does not remove the legal duty to prevent dealing. Product approval should document which sanctions actions are technically possible, who can authorise them, how wrong action is reversed, how reserves and customer entitlements are protected, and what happens when a foreign custodian or decentralised system cannot execute the required control.

TFS effectiveness is measured by speed and accuracy together. “Without delay” is defeated by stale lists, weekend gaps, manual escalation without authority or uncertainty over token control. Legality is defeated by secret private lists, indefinite unresolved holds, failure to examine ownership, or denial of statutory expenses and review. A well-designed regime makes urgent action possible because the legal basis, escalation, technical custody and correction route were built before the alert.

11.7 Travel Rule Legal Baseline

The Travel Rule connects identity and transfer data that a blockchain address alone does not supply. VAA section 47 requires a licensee, for a transfer meeting or exceeding the threshold prescribed by PVARA, to obtain, hold and transmit originator and beneficiary information in a manner consistent with FATF standards. It requires compliance with applicable data-protection, data-governance and cybersecurity law, permits PVARA to prescribe procedures, standards and formats, and requires retention no shorter than the AMLA period. The enacted duty is real; its domestic numerical trigger and operating protocol remain incomplete until valid final rules prescribe them.236

FATF’s 2019 guidance supplies the baseline design. For a qualifying VA transfer, the ordering VASP should obtain and hold accurate required originator information and required beneficiary information and submit that information immediately and securely to the beneficiary VASP or financial institution. The beneficiary VASP should obtain and hold it. FATF used USD/EUR 1,000 as the occasional-transaction CDD and VA-transfer benchmark, with a reduced mandatory data set at or below that level unless suspicion or another requirement applies. The data should not be exposed on a public ledger merely because the value transfer is on-chain.237

A lawful Pakistan data path should identify each stage:

StageActorMinimum functional dataControl
pre-transferordering VASPcustomer/account identifier, originator name and required account/address/identity field; beneficiary name and account/address or transaction identifier; asset, chain, amount and intended counterparty VASPCDD current; sanctions and risk screening; threshold/aggregation calculation
counterparty discoveryordering and beneficiary VASPlegal name, jurisdiction, licence/status, endpoint, security certificate and message capabilitycounterparty due diligence; no reliance on a network label alone
transmissionordering VASPrequired originator/beneficiary message linked unambiguously to the transferimmediate, secure, encrypted, authenticated and integrity-protected channel
receiptbeneficiary VASPmessage receipt, match to pending transfer and missing/invalid-field statusaccept, hold, reject, return or escalate under prescribed risk-based rules
executionrelevant VASP(s)transaction hash or internal transfer reference, time, amount and dispositionTravel Rule data need not be on-chain but must remain reliably linked
post-transfereach VASPfull message, changes, exceptions, communications and monitoring dispositionretention, access restriction, audit log, STR/TFS route and lawful disclosure

The originator data set should distinguish name; account number or unique transaction identifier; and the additional identity field or fields required by the adopted standard, such as address, national identity or customer identification number, or date and place of birth. The beneficiary set should include name and account number, wallet address or other unique transaction identifier. Pakistan’s draft regulation adopts exactly that tripartite shape — originator name, plus account number or wallet address or other unique transaction identifier, plus such additional identifiers as applicable law may require; and for the beneficiary, name plus account number, wallet address or other unique transaction identifier. As far as it goes, that is faithful to the international baseline.238

It is not, however, a specification. A final Pakistan instrument should specify which fields are mandatory above and below the domestic threshold, field syntax, character set, legal-person identifiers, name-screening quality, address formats, multi-asset identifiers and error codes. “FATF compliant” is not a data dictionary. The practical question a rule-maker must answer is which dictionary Pakistan adopts. The interVASP Messaging Standard, IVMS 101, is the interoperability format most widely implemented for this purpose; adopting it expressly — or naming an alternative and publishing a mapping — would resolve at a stroke the field-syntax, transliteration, name-order and legal-person-identifier questions that otherwise fall to each licensee to answer differently. No Pakistani instrument presently names any schema. Until one does, two compliant Pakistani VASPs can exchange a message that each considers well-formed and neither can parse, and the duty in section 47 will have been formally discharged while achieving nothing. Naming the schema is a small drafting act with disproportionate operational return.

Travel Rule data should move separately but synchronously with the value-transfer instruction. Putting personal information in calldata, a token memo or another permanent public field can make it globally visible, immutable and difficult to correct. A secure off-chain messaging protocol, direct bilateral channel or other mechanism can comply if it authenticates the parties, protects confidentiality and integrity, links the message to the transfer, preserves availability, supports correction and records the decision. PVARA should permit interoperable methods that meet outcomes rather than mandate one private vendor.

Accordingly, keeping personally identifiable information off-chain should be the privacy-by-design default for regulatory standards and system architecture unless a defined lawful purpose, necessity assessment and technical safeguard justify another treatment. That is a recommended design standard, not a statement that present Pakistani law imposes an absolute prohibition on every on-chain personal-data field.

Counterparty-VASP due diligence is distinct from customer CDD. Before relying on another provider, a licensee should verify the provider’s legal identity, relevant jurisdiction and permission, physical or accountable presence, AML supervisor, ownership/control, sanctions exposure, Travel Rule capability, security, data location, breach history, response route and treatment of missing information. A foreign registration or network membership is evidence, not a passport into Pakistan. The intensity should reflect volume and risk and should be refreshed when status changes.

Missing or late data requires controlled choices. Final rules should prohibit a mechanical universal answer—always execute, always reject, or always freeze—because the legal consequence depends on amount, suspicion, sanctions, customer risk, reason for failure, counterparty quality and whether the message can be cured. The beneficiary VASP should be able to hold a transfer in a segregated pending state, request missing information, reject or return it, restrict the counterparty, apply enhanced monitoring or file an STR. A sanctions match uses the separate TFS route and cannot wait for ordinary remediation.

Data protection is part of compliance, not an exception to it. VAA section 49 limits collection, use and sharing to necessary or lawful purposes and requires informed consent for non-essential processing. Travel Rule processing should instead be anchored in the statutory obligation, necessity and the applicable lawful-transfer basis; consent should not be presented as freely optional where refusal prevents a legally required transfer. The VASP should minimise fields, encrypt data in transit and at rest, segregate Travel Rule and marketing uses, control staff access, test vendors, manage foreign transfers, notify breaches as required, honour lawful correction and deletion subject to retention/legal holds, and document privacy and security assessments.239

FATF’s 2025 targeted update found that implementation and enforcement of the Travel Rule remained incomplete across jurisdictions. That fact counsels a managed interoperability period, not postponement of Pakistan’s rule. PVARA should publish conformance tests, message examples, counterparty-failure handling and a staged transition, while retaining direct supervisory access to evidence of compliance rather than to unrestricted customer data.240

11.8 Threshold Precision and Cross-Border Interoperability

There is no universal domestic Travel Rule threshold. FATF’s benchmark is USD/EUR 1,000. United States funds-transfer rules, as explained by FinCEN, generally apply the funds Travel Rule to transmittals of funds of USD 3,000 or more and require specified transmittor and recipient information. Other jurisdictions use their own legislation, including zero-threshold or different data approaches. The foreign rule binds through its own legal nexus; it does not become Pakistan law merely because a counterparty VASP applies it.241

VAA section 47 assigns Pakistan’s threshold to PVARA. Draft regulation 100 proposes, pending prescription, the PKR equivalent of USD/EUR 1,000. Because PVARA’s official page states that the draft is not final and is subject to revision, that proposal cannot be represented as the operative domestic number. The final instrument should identify its parent power and publication/effective date and specify:

  • the number and currency or benchmark, including whether different data obligations apply above and below it;
  • the authoritative conversion source, valuation timestamp, treatment of spreads and unavailable/stale prices;
  • asset identification, including wrapped assets, stable-value assets, illiquid tokens and transfers with several assets;
  • aggregation of linked transfers by customer, beneficiary, counterparty, device, address and time window;
  • anti-structuring treatment, while preserving the independent suspicion test at every amount;
  • which event measures the threshold—order, acceptance, broadcast, confirmation, settlement or credit;
  • treatment of internal ledger transfers, failed transactions, fee-only transfers, refunds, returns, batching, UTXO change and smart-contract interactions;
  • responsibilities where more than one VASP participates, or where a bank or payment provider controls a fiat leg;
  • rules for unavailable or conflicting counterparty requirements; and
  • change control, notice, grandfathering and machine-readable publication.

Thresholds ration a minimum data duty; they do not create a safe harbour. A transfer below the number remains subject to sanctions, suspicion, CDD where otherwise triggered, monitoring and any verified customer data requirement. A transfer above it does not become suspicious by amount alone. The system should record both the threshold decision and the independent risk decision.

Cross-border interoperability also requires a conflict rule. The ordering VASP may face Pakistan’s minimum fields, a beneficiary jurisdiction’s additional fields, privacy or localisation restrictions and a counterparty protocol’s technical requirements. The final rules should permit additional necessary fields where lawfully required, but require the VASP to identify the legal basis, minimise data and prevent foreign commercial preferences from silently expanding collection for all Pakistani customers. If transfer is legally impossible, the entity should reject or return it with an auditable reason rather than leak data through an insecure workaround.

FATF revised Recommendation 16 in June 2025 and stated that the changes should apply by the end of 2030. Pakistan’s present rule should therefore be standards-aware but legally time-correct: implement the current VAA and applicable FATF baseline now, design fields and systems that can migrate, and amend the domestic instrument through lawful process when the revised international requirements become applicable. A future standard cannot be backdated into a present offence or sanction.242

The transition should use a published “sunrise” sequence: final rule and schema; provider registration; test environment; bilateral and network conformance; production for high-capability corridors; monitored exception period; full enforcement; and periodic review. Each stage should identify what duty applies, what evidence PVARA will inspect and what happens when a foreign provider cannot receive the message. Delay should not be disguised as permanent “testing”, and early participants should not be sanctioned for requirements that were unpublished or technically unavailable.243

11.9 Self-Hosted Wallets, DeFi and Control Tests

A transfer involving a self-hosted or unhosted wallet has only one regulated VASP endpoint. It does not have no identifiable actor: the VASP still knows its customer and can collect the intended counterparty, purpose, wallet, asset and transaction information. It also does not automatically have a second VASP capable of receiving a Travel Rule message. Final rules should recognise that difference rather than deem the customer to be a VASP or prohibit the transfer categorically.

Risk-based controls can include obtaining the counterparty’s name and wallet address, checking sanctions and transaction exposure, asking the customer about purpose and relationship, testing wallet control where proportionate, applying limits or enhanced review, and monitoring the completed transaction. A cryptographic signature, micro-transaction or other proof can show control of a wallet credential; it does not prove legal identity, beneficial ownership, lawful source or freedom from compromise. Proof methods should not create disproportionate surveillance or force customers to reveal unrelated wallet history.

Restrictions require evidence and a source. A privacy-enhancing asset, mixer exposure, bridge, peer-to-peer transfer or self-hosted wallet may increase opacity or complicate counterparty verification in particular facts. None is inherently proof of laundering. The VASP should record the exposure path, timing, value, service attribution, model confidence, customer explanation and other facts. It may then apply enhanced controls, decline an unsupported risk, or report suspicion. A private vendor’s label should not become an unpublished prohibition of general application.244

“DeFi” similarly describes architecture, not a legal exemption or legal person. FATF’s functional approach asks whether creators, owners, operators or other persons retain control or sufficient influence and perform VASP functions, even where software presents itself as decentralised. The analysis should test:

Control surfaceEvidence to examineRegulatory significance
upgrade, pause, mint, seize or parameter keyskey holders, replacement power, multisig quorum and actual useability to control core service or customer exposure
front-end and APIoperator, geoblocking, fees, order routing and custody connectionsperformance or facilitation of covered service for users
treasury and fee switchbeneficial recipients, discretionary allocation and revenue dependenceeconomic control and service business evidence
governancetoken concentration, delegation, veto, quorum, off-chain agreements and emergency councilseffective influence, not merely formal voting percentages
oracle, bridge and validator dependenciesselection, replacement, concentration and contractual controloperational control and third-party risk
development and brandcompany/foundation role, employment, repositories, marketing and user commitmentsrelevant context but not alone conclusive

The conclusion must identify a person and covered activity. Code cannot file an STR, appoint an MLRO, receive notice or exercise an appeal. If no person performs or controls the regulated service on the evidence, calling the protocol a VASP does not solve supervision. If an identifiable person does, “decentralised” branding does not remove the duty.245

VASP interaction with DeFi should still be controlled where no DeFi operator is regulated. Product approval should evaluate contract risk, administrator powers, sanctions and illicit-finance exposure, oracle and bridge dependencies, liquidity, transaction finality, customer disclosure, monitoring coverage, custody consequences and incident response. The control is placed on the licensed entity’s decision to provide access or transfer; it should not claim jurisdiction over a technical protocol beyond the statute.

11.10 Investigations, Seizure and Evidentiary Custody

Financial-integrity systems generate leads and preserve records; they do not confer every investigative power on PVARA, FMU or a VASP. VAA sections 50–61 create offences, investigation and enforcement mechanisms, administrative sanctions, emergency intervention and blocking powers. AMLA gives FMU information and temporary-freeze functions and assigns investigation/prosecution to authorised agencies. PECA, criminal procedure, evidence law and mutual legal assistance supply further source-specific tools. The actor must identify the power before compelling data, freezing control, searching a device or moving an asset.246

For a digital asset, preservation has two objects: evidence and value. Moving value to a secure wallet may protect it from dissipation but creates a new transaction, fees, tax/accounting questions, key risk and possible contamination of the evidential narrative. Leaving value in place may preserve the original state but allow the controller to move it. An operational protocol should therefore require a lawful order and document:

  • legal authority, offence or proceeding, issuing actor, time, scope and review route;
  • asset, network, chain identifier, contract, token ID, quantity, address and transaction hash;
  • block height, confirmations, timestamp source, explorer/node and method of acquisition;
  • legal owner, alleged beneficial owner, customer entitlement, custodian and persons with key or account control;
  • key type, device, seed phrase, hardware wallet, multisignature quorum, administrator key and recovery method, without unnecessarily reproducing secrets;
  • valuation source and time, forks, airdrops, staking rewards, rebases, fees and other changes;
  • internal-ledger balances, fiat leg, Travel Rule message, CDD, alerts, STR access restrictions and communications;
  • preservation hash, forensic image, export format, software/version, analyst steps and chain of custody;
  • whether value was frozen, seized, transferred, converted or only observed, and the authority for each act; and
  • protection of unaffected customer assets, return, expenses, forfeiture, disposal and appeal.

Possession of a key is not possession of an exclusive physical object. A seed can have undisclosed copies; a multisignature wallet requires a quorum; an exchange account may be changed through internal administration without an on-chain signature. Investigators should secure devices, credentials and recovery routes proportionately, change control only where authorised, prevent employees or vendors from retaining unilateral access, and test the destination custody before transfer. A “government wallet” without governance, segregation, reconciliation and independent audit recreates the custody risk it was meant to cure.

PECA section 31 permits expedited preservation of specified data reasonably required for a criminal investigation where it risks modification, loss, destruction or inaccessibility, subject to written notice and prompt court oversight. Sections 33–35 provide warrant-based search, seizure, access, copying, intelligible output and technical assistance for offences within that Act; section 39 governs court-ordered real-time collection with specificity, necessity, time and third-party privacy controls. The Qanun-e-Shahadat recognises relevant electronic records from functioning automated systems, expert evidence on authenticity and integrity, proof of security procedures and evidence available through modern devices. These rules make provenance and integrity part of proof, not a clerical afterthought.247

Cross-border location is normal in virtual-asset cases. A customer may be in Pakistan, the VASP incorporated elsewhere, keys held by a sub-custodian, servers in a third country and value transferable globally. The Mutual Legal Assistance (Criminal Matters) Act 2020 allows Pakistan to request documents, search, freezing/seizure, tracing and transmission through the central authority; it also permits expedited preservation of electronic data and court-ordered production, search and seizure on incoming requests. Informal FIU, regulator or investigator cooperation can preserve speed and intelligence, but compulsory production, restraint and evidential use must follow the applicable legal channel and conditions.248

The case file must preserve state transitions. An alert becomes a reasoned suspicion; an STR becomes FMU intelligence; intelligence may support an investigation; an investigation may produce admissible evidence; an allegation may result in a finding or acquittal. A sanctions designation can independently trigger a freeze. Recording those transitions protects both effectiveness and fairness and prevents a high-risk label from being presented in court as if it were proof of the predicate offence.

11.11 Effectiveness, Proportionality and Exclusion

Compliance volume is not effectiveness. Counts of customers rejected, alerts created, STRs filed or transfers blocked can rise because controls are badly tuned. An effective system should measure whether risks were understood, significant cases were detected promptly, reports were useful, assets were lawfully preserved, false positives were corrected, sanctions obligations were met, weak entities were remediated and excluded customers had access to reasoned correction.

A balanced performance set should include:

  • completeness and timeliness of CDD and beneficial-ownership refresh;
  • monitoring coverage across on-chain and internal-ledger activity;
  • alert-to-investigation and investigation-to-STR rates by rule, with false-positive and override analysis;
  • STR timeliness, narrative quality, supporting-data completeness and FMU feedback;
  • sanctions-list ingestion latency, potential-match resolution time, confirmed-match action time and erroneous-freeze correction;
  • Travel Rule data completeness, message success, counterparty failures and pending-transfer age;
  • goAML rejection/error rates and entity onboarding status;
  • supervisory findings, repeat breaches, remediation age and outcomes of appeals;
  • de-risking by customer type, geography and product, including unexplained concentration; and
  • enforcement progression from suspicion to investigation, charge, finding, conviction, release and forfeiture, without treating attrition alone as failure.

Proportionality means controls should increase with demonstrated risk and reduce where risk is lower, while statutory minima remain. FATF’s 2025 revisions emphasised proportionality and financial inclusion. That direction matters in Pakistan, where categorical exclusion of small businesses, overseas Pakistanis, humanitarian activity, rural users or customers associated with a region can push transactions into less visible channels. Financial inclusion is not a waiver; it is a design constraint requiring simplified measures where legally available, tiered products, limits, alternative reliable identity, enhanced monitoring and a route to full CDD.249

De-risking must be governed. A VASP may decline or exit a relationship it cannot understand or control, but group labels should not substitute for customer evidence. Decisions should identify the legal or risk basis, senior approval where material, treatment of customer assets, withdrawal or return path, confidentiality limits and complaint or appeal route. AMLA section 7J provides an appeal to the concerned AML/CFT regulatory authority for a person aggrieved by a reporting entity’s CDD or business-relationship decision. That remedy cannot function for the VASP sector unless the competent supervisor is unambiguously designated and able to receive it.250

Rights also improve detection. A customer who can correct a false name match, outdated beneficial owner or broken Travel Rule message prevents bad data from propagating. A protected analyst who can challenge a vendor score prevents automation bias. An independent sanctions appeal and documented administrative process expose weak rules. Confidentiality remains essential: a right to reasons may be limited to avoid tipping off or prejudicing an investigation, but the limitation should be source-specific and no broader than necessary.

Effectiveness review should be periodic and empirical. PVARA, FMU and the National AML/CFT Authority should publish aggregate outcomes without revealing STRs or investigative methods, commission thematic reviews, compare regulatory data with case outcomes, test entity systems and retire rules that create noise without useful intelligence. The question is not whether the framework looks severe. It is whether it produces accurate, lawful and timely action.

11.12 Corrective Financial-Integrity Package

Pakistan has a primary statutory foundation: the AML bridge, direct VASP and issuer duties, a Travel Rule baseline, reporting interfaces and data limits. Completion requires the following controlled package:

Instrument or actionMinimum contentEvidence of completion
AMLA Schedule IV instrumentpublish any existing PVARA notification, or notify PVARA under Schedule IV item 1(vi); allocate s 6A supervision, concurrent SBP/SECP work and s 7J appealsGazette/SRO text and updated official consolidation
issuer amendmentreporting-entity status, supervisor, CDD/records, FMU channel, sanctions, confidentiality and appeal for every s 46(2) issuerenacted amendment and commencement
VAA technical correctionreplace the anomalous “FMLI” reference with the intended institution; preserve FMU, TFS, investigation and court functionsamending Act251
final PVARA RegulationsMLRO; enterprise/customer risk; CDD/beneficial ownership; monitoring and goAML; cash-only CTR treatment; UN/domestic TFS and CPF; records, privacy, cyber, vendors, inspection, sanctions and transitionfinal notified text and consultation response252
Travel Rule specificationdomestic threshold; named data schema (IVMS 101 or a named alternative with published mapping); fields; valuation, aggregation and structuring; counterparty due diligence; missing data; self-hosted wallets; cross-border conflict; security and retentionmachine-readable schema, test cases and commencement
functions protocolPVARA–FMU–National Authority–SBP–SECP–MOFA–Ministry of Interior/provincial Home Departments–NACTA–investigator hand-offs, each tied to a statute, lawful data set, confidentiality, response time and correction; separate the UN (1948 Act/SRO 261(I)/2019) and domestic ATA designation routes explicitlysigned public protocol with protected operational annex

The functions protocol must not create powers. FMU should lead STR/CTR receipt, goAML and intelligence; PVARA should lead VASP preventive supervision after valid AMLA allocation; SBP and SECP should lead their sectoral perimeters with joint-examination rules; the National AML/CFT Authority should lead strategy and performance; competent UN and ATA institutions should lead their separate TFS routes; authorised agencies and courts should lead compulsion, restraint and adjudication.

Technical completion requires entity-level goAML verification, secure credentials, test and production approval, reconciliation between the public licence register and confidential reporting register, and an interoperable Travel Rule conformance suite. Supervision should sample actual onboarding, beneficial ownership, alerts, STR narratives, sanctions matches, Travel Rule failures, model changes, frozen-asset custody and customer exits. Significant compliance sanctions should state facts, law, outcome and appeal status without exposing STRs or investigations.253

Every NOC, sandbox and incumbent file should state authorised activity, conditions, AML supervisor, goAML status, deadline and customer treatment. A draft threshold or private schema is not enforceable law. Completion is proved by the Schedule IV instrument, final Regulations and specification, functions protocol, conformance record and first effectiveness report—not by consultation closure or a target date.254

That last point is no longer hypothetical. The consultation on the VASP Regulations opened on 11 June 2026 and closed on 2 July 2026; at the date of this chapter it has been closed for some seven weeks, PVARA's own instrument register still shows no final Regulations, no threshold has been prescribed under section 47, and no Schedule IV notification has been located. Each of those is individually curable by a single instrument. Together they mean that the operative components of Pakistan's virtual-asset financial-integrity regime — who supervises, at what transfer value the duty bites, and in what format the data must move — presently rest on a lapsed consultation rather than on law. The Act has done its work; the delegated legislation has not.255

The result is exact. Deeming creates obligation; designation completes the supervisor. On-chain visibility is not identity. goAML is the reporting channel, not the suspicion test. Travel Rule data must travel securely but need not be written on-chain. AML and TFS may share data, but not a decision rule. A risk signal begins an enquiry; lawful evidence supports an outcome.

Consolidation record. This revision consolidates the canonical v0.21 chapter with the legacy standalone treatment (`pakistan-digital-assets-chapter-12.md`, 12 August 2026, “AML/CFT, Sanctions, Travel Rule, and Technical Standards”) and the `work/chapter-10` research file. Four propositions from the legacy text were adopted after independent sourcing: the two-route sanctions architecture with named resolutions; the identity of the proscribing authority; the naming of a Travel Rule message schema; and the Schedule IV completion gap. Four were rejected as unsupported and are recorded in the accompanying Consolidation and Audit Ledger: the DNFBP-to-financial-institution “elevation” narrative; a seven-year record-retention figure with no statutory basis; the assertion that the ATA freeze bypasses judicial or administrative review; and a set of operational controls (micro-transfer proof, message-signing, WORM storage, IVMS 101 as existing law, “Regulation 12.2”, “PVARA-Form A7”) attributed to instruments that do not contain them.

-**The seizure protocol in operational terms.** The Drive publication text records a Digital Asset Seizure standard operating procedure in four elements, which are recovered here because they translate the documentary requirements above into instructions an investigating officer can actually follow: **[CONSOLIDATED — Drive Doc, 17 Aug 2026]**
-- **Hardware isolation.** Physical hardware — devices, hardware wallets, backup media — is seized into anti-static Faraday bags, so that the device cannot receive a remote wipe instruction or a network signal between seizure and examination.
-- **Bit-stream forensic imaging.** A raw disk image is taken and hashed using SHA-256, the hash being recorded at the point of acquisition. Article 78-A of the *Qanun-e-Shahadat Order 1984* supplies the evidentiary route by which the integrity of that image is later proved.
-- **Air-gapped multisignature custody.** Seized tokens are moved, where movement is authorised, into government-controlled vaults operated on an air-gapped multisignature quorum, so that no single official can transfer the asset and no signing key is exposed to a networked machine.
-- **Forensic tool accreditation.** Tools used for acquisition and analysis are accredited in compliance with the *National Forensics Agency Act, 2024*.
-Two cautions attach to this protocol, and they are the reason it belongs in a legal chapter rather than a technical annex. **[DEEPENED — 19 Aug 2026]** First, hashing proves that an image has not changed since the hash was taken; it does not prove that the image was lawfully obtained, that the device belonged to the accused, or that the accused authorised any transaction the image records. -## 11.1 Risk and Legal Architecture
-Financial-integrity law loses accuracy when different legal states are compressed into the word “risk”. Suspicion is not guilt. A report is not a charge. A sanctions-screening match is not identity. A blockchain-analytics score is not proof. A freeze is not forfeiture. A VASP licence is not, by itself, a complete allocation of AML supervision. Each state has a different actor, legal trigger, info
-Pakistan’s starting point is nevertheless stronger than a voluntary or guidance-only model. Section 46 of the *Virtual Assets Act 2026* deems a licensed VASP to be a “financial institution” for purposes of the *Anti-Money Laundering Act 2010*. It directly requires every VASP and issuer to report suspicious transactions to the Financial Monitoring Unit (FMU), keep customer-due-diligence and transa
-The legal architecture is therefore a chain, not a single statute:
-| Layer | Controlling actor or instrument | Legal work performed | What it does not establish |

-| investigation and adjudication | FMU dissemination, authorised agencies, prosecutors and courts under source-specific law | preservation, production, search, seizure, proof, trial and forfeiture | retrospective validation of an unlawful private or public intervention |
-| international benchmark | FATF Recommendations and guidance | common outcomes, interoperability and effectiveness tests | self-executing Pakistani law or a universal domestic threshold |
-AMLA makes the FMU Pakistan’s financial-intelligence unit. It receives and analyses STRs and CTRs, may call for records, disseminates financial intelligence under confidentiality controls, maintains domestic and foreign linkages, and permits the Director General in the conditions of section 6(6) to order a temporary freeze for up to fifteen days. Section 6A assigns preventive supervision to the r
-The National AML/CFT Authority, established in 2023, is the policy and coordination body for strategy, action plans, legislative review, international engagement and performance. It can expose institutional gaps; it cannot merge member institutions or reallocate coercive powers by committee decision.[^217]
-Risk assessment must be dated and scoped. Pakistan’s 2023 NRA assessed VAs/VASPs as an “unregulated emerging area” only to the extent of available data and rated virtual currency as a medium terrorist-financing channel. It is not a 2026 finding that every licensed VASP, token or wallet is high risk.[^218]
-Every control must answer: **who owes it; what triggers it; what data moves to which institution; what action follows; and how error is corrected**.
-## 11.2 Reporting-Entity and VASP Coverage
-The VAA uses a direct statutory bridge for licensed VASPs. Section 46(1) says they are deemed financial institutions for AMLA purposes. That is important because AMLA’s pre-existing financial-institution definition is activity based—it includes money or value transfer, payment means, safekeeping or administration of cash or liquid securities, management of another person’s funds, financial interm
-Coverage must still be stated by legal status and activity:
-| Actor or arrangement | Financial-integrity position | Required control |
-|---|---|---|
-| PVARA-licensed VASP | deemed AMLA financial institution; direct VAA s 46 duties | full AML/CFT/CPF programme, CDD, records, monitoring, STR reporting, TFS and Travel Rule when prescribed |
-| person holding an interim NOC, sandbox admission or incubation approval | depends on the exact instrument and transition clause; not automatically identical to a final licence | verify instrument, scope, conditions, reporting-entity basis, goAML registration and transition deadline before operation |
-| issuer that is also a licensed VASP | both statuses apply; duties may overlap | one controlled programme with product-specific issuer and transfer risks, without double counting reports |
-| issuer that is not a licensed VASP | VAA s 46(2) directly names issuers, but the AMLA reporting-entity, supervisor, sanctions and protection route requires express completion | primary or valid delegated bridge identifying supervisor, FMU channel, CDD/record duties, sanctions and appeals |
-| bank, EMI, payment provider, broker or securities intermediary dealing with VAs | remains within SBP or SECP perimeter in addition to any VASP status | coordinated supervision; no lowest-standard arbitrage |
-| foreign VASP serving Pakistan | VAA territorial and licensing rules apply where the statutory nexus is met; foreign licensing does not displace Pakistan law | local permission and accountable presence or enforceable cooperation, plus counterparty due diligence |
-| pure software, self-hosted wallet user or genuinely decentralised protocol | not a VASP merely because technology facilitates transfers | control and activity test; regulate the person performing covered services, not code as if it were a legal person |
-The issuer sentence exposes a real plumbing problem. Section 46(2) directly orders every “Virtual Asset Service Provider and Issuer” to report STRs, retain records and maintain controls. But AMLA defines a reporting entity as a financial institution, DNFBP or other notified person, while VAA section 46(1) deems only licensed VASPs—not every issuer—to be a financial institution. -The status the Act confers must also be stated precisely, because an earlier and still-circulating account of Pakistan's position is wrong for the law in force. Whatever the position under the lapsed *Virtual Assets
-There is a related regulator-allocation problem, and it is more acute than a missing notification. The official AMLA consolidation inspected for this chapter lists SBP, SECP, FBR, the National Savings supervisory board, the Pakistan Post supervisory board and — at item 1(vi) — "any other such entity or regulatory authority as may be notified by the Federal Government". That consolidation is updat
-Transitional labels require equal discipline. PVARA's official consultation page says the 2026 VASP Regulations are a draft, not final, and subject to revision; the consultation itself ran from 11 June to 2 July 2026 and has closed, and PVARA's regulations register still lists only the Act, the No Objection Certificate Regulations and the Incubation Guidelines for the Regulatory Sandbox. -Perimeter control should be functional and anti-evasive. Splitting exchange, custody and transfer across related companies does not eliminate group risk; nor does outsourcing screening or Travel Rule messaging eliminate the licensed entity’s duty.
