-## 11.3 Risk Assessment and Customer Due Diligence
-AMLA requires CDD when a reporting entity enters a business relationship, conducts an occasional transaction above the prescribed threshold, encounters suspicion regardless of exemptions or thresholds, or doubts previously obtained information. It requires identity verification from reliable and independent sources, identification and reasonable verification of the beneficial owner, understanding
-For a VASP, those rules should operate across an enterprise risk assessment and a customer risk assessment. The enterprise assessment should consider at least:
-- authorised services and actual transaction patterns, not merely licence labels;
-- custody model, private-key and administrator-key concentration, smart-contract upgrade powers and reliance on third-party wallets;
-- customer types, beneficial-ownership opacity, PEP exposure, legal-person and arrangement use, nominees and cross-border groups;
-- asset characteristics, including transferability, liquidity, privacy features, governance, issuer or reserve structure, bridge and mixer exposure, without declaring a technology inherently illicit;
-- delivery channels, remote onboarding, devices, account recovery, API access, agents and introducers;
-- geographic exposure, current sanctions and FATF statements, legal interoperability and counterparty-VASP quality;
-- fiat entry and exit, bank and payment partners, cash exposure, OTC desks and mule-account indicators;
-- fraud, cyber compromise, ransomware, market abuse, tax-crime and proliferation-financing typologies that may generate predicate or associated risk; and
-- data confidence, model limitations, false-positive rates and the availability of reliable independent verification.
-The customer assessment then asks what those factors mean for the actual relationship. Standard CDD should obtain the natural person’s verified identity and contact information, expected purpose, occupation or business, source of funds where risk or product requires it, wallet and account relationships, expected volume and geography, beneficial owner and controller, and the authority of anyone ac
-Enhanced due diligence is a response to higher risk, not a euphemism for automatic refusal. Measures may include stronger identity proof, independent corporate documents, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds corroboration, senior approval, shorter review cycles, transaction limits, wallet ownership/control testing, counterparty-VASP verification, deeper reserve or issuer inquiry and enhanced moni
-Reliance and outsourcing must preserve accountability. A VASP may use an identity vendor, blockchain-analytics provider, Travel Rule network, foreign affiliate or bank information where law permits, but should know what was checked, obtain the underlying evidence without delay, test the provider, understand geographic and model limits, control subcontracting and retain a fallback. A vendor’s “ver
-FATF’s 2019 guidance supplies a useful benchmark: apply CDD to occasional VA transactions above USD/EUR 1,000, use risk-based enhanced controls rather than categorical assumptions, and coordinate Travel Rule implementation with privacy and data-protection authorities. It remains guidance, not Pakistan’s threshold rule. The VAA deliberately leaves Pakistan’s transfer trigger to PVARA; final rules
-CDD is therefore a continuing evidential process. An address check at onboarding does not control a relationship after a change in ownership, device, product, transaction pattern or sanctions exposure. VASPs should define event-driven refresh triggers as well as periodic review. A change should record its source, reviewer, effect on risk, information obtained and any monitoring consequence. They
-## 11.4 Beneficial Ownership and Control
-AMLA defines a beneficial owner as the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a customer, or on whose behalf a transaction is conducted, including a person exercising ultimate effective control over a legal person or legal arrangement. The enquiry therefore ends with a natural person unless the applicable law provides a carefully defined fallback after documented exhaustion. A company nam
-Virtual-asset systems add technical control facts that must be connected to, but not confused with, legal ownership:
-| Control fact | What it can show | What further question remains |
-|---|---|---|
-| signature from a private key | present ability to authorise a transaction | whether the signer owns the asset or acts lawfully for another |
-| custody account in a customer’s name | platform attribution and contractual account | whether the named person is the beneficial owner and whether the platform controls an omnibus wallet |
-| multisignature membership | part of the approval quorum | who selects members, changes quorum, replaces keys or directs votes |
-| smart-contract administrator or upgrade key | ability to change, pause, mint, seize or redirect the system | who ultimately controls the administrator and under what legal duty |
-| governance-token concentration | possible influence over protocol decisions | delegation, coordination, vetoes, off-chain control and whether service activity is actually performed |
-| proof-of-control message from a self-hosted wallet | control of the signing credential at that time | identity, beneficial ownership, source of assets and compromise/coercion risk |
-| transaction-graph association | technical relationship or exposure under the vendor’s model | attribution, timing, amount, model assumptions and innocent explanations |
-For licensed entities, beneficial-ownership analysis should connect four maps: legal ownership; voting and appointment rights; economic entitlement; and operational/technical control. VAA controller thresholds and licensing disclosures can identify formal controllers, but an AML enquiry should also capture acting-in-concert arrangements, side agreements, financing dependence, nominees and persons
-The same method applies to customers. For a corporate treasury using several wallets, the VASP should identify the company’s natural-person beneficial owner, the authorised officers, the persons able to sign or reset credentials, and the purpose of each wallet. For a trust or arrangement, it should identify the statutory beneficial-ownership parties and separately record who controls the relevant
-The PVARA consultation draft proposes an MLRO, enterprise risk assessment, CDD, analytics governance, transaction monitoring, Travel Rule, targeted-financial-sanctions and record-keeping controls. Those proposals are directionally useful because they link legal duties with virtual-asset operations. They are not final law and cannot repair a primary-law gap by assertion. The final instrument shoul
-False precision is a particular danger. A protocol can be influenced through a foundation, development company, validator concentration, front-end, fee switch, oracle, treasury, governance delegation, upgrade key or dominant commercial relationship. “Decentralised” is not dispositive, but neither is participation in development enough to establish control. The question is whether an identifiable
-Beneficial-ownership records must be refreshable and reconcilable. Changes in corporate registries, shareholder agreements, wallet signers, administrator keys, governance delegation or adverse information should trigger review. Where information conflicts, the VASP should resolve the inconsistency or restrict the relationship and consider reporting; it should not merely store contradictory docume
-## 11.5 Transaction Monitoring, STR/CTR and goAML
-AMLA section 7 requires a reporting entity to file an STR promptly where it knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect that a transaction or pattern involves proceeds, evades AMLA requirements, lacks an apparent lawful purpose after examination of available facts, or involves terrorist financing. All CTRs must be filed within seven working days. The 2025 reporting regulations require examination o
-The monitoring lifecycle should be auditable from event to outcome:
-| Stage | Minimum record | Decision control |
-|---|---|---|
-| data capture | customer/account, asset, chain, address, transaction hash, time, amount and valuation, fiat leg, device/API, counterparty and Travel Rule fields | completeness, clock and asset-identifier checks |
-| alert | rule/model version, factor, threshold, source data and generated time | no adverse action solely because an opaque vendor score exists |
-| triage | obvious data or list errors, duplicate alerts, customer context, exposure path and urgency | priority rules; independent sanctions route where applicable |
-| investigation | transaction pattern, beneficial owner, source/destination, off-chain records, customer explanation, prior alerts and linked accounts | proportionate information request; no tipping off |
-| disposition | reasoned close, enhanced monitoring, restriction, exit, STR, sanctions action or law-enforcement preservation | authorised reviewer and conflict control |
-| report | statutory trigger, narrative, actors, chronology, identifiers, amounts, supporting documents and urgency | submit to FMU alone through the required confidential route |
-| feedback and tuning | FMU/regulator feedback, confirmed typology, false positives and missed cases | controlled model change with validation and approval |
-On-chain and off-chain information must be joined. A public ledger can show that an address sent a quantity of a token to another address at a time and block height. It may not show the natural person, authority, source of funds, reason for transfer, internal platform allocation, fiat leg or whether the transaction succeeded economically. An internal ledger can show customer attribution and net b
-A system alert is not yet statutory suspicion. The reporting entity should examine the available facts and state the reason for its disposition. It need not prove the predicate offence before reporting. Equally, it should not file defensive reports containing unanalysed transaction dumps simply because a vendor label is severe. The narrative should tell FMU what happened, why it is suspicious, wh
-CTR must remain separate. Under the 2025 regulations it is a report of a **cash transaction** at or above the threshold specified by the National Executive Committee, filed within seven working days. A VA transfer is not transformed into cash because its value exceeds a benchmark. Where an OTC transaction has a physical-cash leg, the cash report may apply; where it is purely on-chain, the relevan
-goAML is the FMU submission and data-exchange software. It is not the legal test for suspicion, a public accusation register, or automatic permission for every agency to browse customer records. The VASP forms the suspicion under law, submits the report through goAML, and protects its confidentiality. FMU analyses and disseminates under its statute. PVARA may receive supervisory information throu
-Confidentiality and retention require category mapping. AMLA protects STR/CTR secrecy and prohibits tipping off; the reporting regulations require assistance to remain confidential. Section 7(4) requires STR/CTR records for ten years, while section 7C generally requires transaction and CDD records for at least five years after the transaction or relationship. -## 11.6 Sanctions, Proliferation Financing and Asset Freezing
-“Sanctions” describes at least two different regimes. The *AML/CFT Sanctions Rules 2020* provide administrative consequences for preventive-compliance failures: monetary penalties, conditions or restrictions, licence revocation, officer disqualification, censure and remedial directions, with proportionality factors, a due-diligence defence, written notice, appeal and publication of significant sa
-Pakistan’s domestic route under the *Anti-Terrorism Act 1997* includes proscription of organisations and persons on statutory grounds and review mechanisms. Section 11O provides, upon proscription, for freezing or seizure without prior notice and without delay of money or other property owned or controlled wholly or jointly, directly or indirectly, including derived property and property of perso
-Two features of that architecture are routinely misdescribed, and both matter operationally. The first is the split between the two designation routes. The United Nations route is grounded in section 2 of the *United Nations (Security Council) Act 1948* and the Federal Government’s implementing order, S.R.O. 261(I)/2019 of 4 March 2019 — the UNSC (Freezing and Seizure) Order 2019 — and is organis
-The second is the identity of the designating authority. Organisations are proscribed by the **Ministry of Interior** under section 11B(1) read with the First Schedule; persons are placed on the **Fourth Schedule** by notification of the provincial Home Department. NACTA publishes, standardises and reconciles those lists and supports implementation, but it is not the proscribing authority and sta
-It should also be said plainly, against a common overstatement, that the ATA freeze is not a power exercised beyond review. It is deliberately ex parte and immediate — that is its point, and prior notice would defeat it — but section 11O(4) requires the Federal Government, on the application of any affected person, to inquire into ownership and control and to order immediate release where propert
-The operational decision sequence should be explicit:
-1. ingest the current official UN and domestic lists through controlled sources and record list version, publication time and ingestion time;
-2. screen customers, beneficial owners, controllers, authorised users, counterparties, addresses and relevant issuers at onboarding, list update and transaction time;
-3. treat a potential name or identifier match as an alert, resolving identity with aliases, date/place of birth, nationality, identifiers, corporate data and other reliable information;
-4. where identity is confirmed or the applicable ownership/control rule is met, act without delay under the correct legal instrument and do not wait for an STR threshold, investigation or conviction;
-5. block prohibited dealing and preserve the affected property and records without treating the property as transferred to the VASP or State;
-6. report through the instrument-specific channels, while making any independently required STR confidentially to FMU;
-7. protect non-designated customer assets, resolve false positives quickly, and provide the applicable review, delisting and expense routes; and
-8. maintain a complete decision and custody record for supervision and proceedings.
-Name screening alone is insufficient. Ownership and control can operate through companies, trusts, nominees, joint property, multisignature arrangements, custodians and persons acting on another’s direction. Conversely, a shared name, remote transaction-graph link or historical receipt from an address does not automatically prove that the current customer is designated or controlled. Both over-fr
-Proliferation financing needs an express module, not a passing reference to terrorist financing. AMLA defines proliferation financing and requires policies and procedures to implement TFS obligations; VAA section 46 requires AML/CFT/CPF controls. A VASP’s assessment should address trade and corporate opacity, dual-use procurement, front companies, sanctions evasion, maritime and logistics indicat
-Issuer and token controls are material. An FRT, ART, tokenised claim or issuer-controlled smart contract may allow minting, redemption, pausing, clawback or blacklisting. The existence of a technical function does not create authority to use it; the absence of one does not remove the legal duty to prevent dealing. Product approval should document which sanctions actions are technically possible,
-TFS effectiveness is measured by speed and accuracy together. “Without delay” is defeated by stale lists, weekend gaps, manual escalation without authority or uncertainty over token control. Legality is defeated by secret private lists, indefinite unresolved holds, failure to examine ownership, or denial of statutory expenses and review. -## 11.8 Threshold Precision and Cross-Border Interoperability
-There is no universal domestic Travel Rule threshold. FATF’s benchmark is USD/EUR 1,000. United States funds-transfer rules, as explained by FinCEN, generally apply the funds Travel Rule to transmittals of funds of USD 3,000 or more and require specified transmittor and recipient information. Other jurisdictions use their own legislation, including zero-threshold or different data approaches. The
-VAA section 47 assigns Pakistan’s threshold to PVARA. Draft regulation 100 proposes, pending prescription, the PKR equivalent of USD/EUR 1,000. Because PVARA’s official page states that the draft is not final and is subject to revision, that proposal cannot be represented as the operative domestic number. The final instrument should identify its parent power and publication/effective date and spe
-- the number and currency or benchmark, including whether different data obligations apply above and below it;
-- the authoritative conversion source, valuation timestamp, treatment of spreads and unavailable/stale prices;
-- asset identification, including wrapped assets, stable-value assets, illiquid tokens and transfers with several assets;
-- aggregation of linked transfers by customer, beneficiary, counterparty, device, address and time window;
-- anti-structuring treatment, while preserving the independent suspicion test at every amount;
-- which event measures the threshold—order, acceptance, broadcast, confirmation, settlement or credit;
-- treatment of internal ledger transfers, failed transactions, fee-only transfers, refunds, returns, batching, UTXO change and smart-contract interactions;
-- responsibilities where more than one VASP participates, or where a bank or payment provider controls a fiat leg;
-- rules for unavailable or conflicting counterparty requirements; and
-- change control, notice, grandfathering and machine-readable publication.
-Thresholds ration a minimum data duty; they do not create a safe harbour. A transfer below the number remains subject to sanctions, suspicion, CDD where otherwise triggered, monitoring and any verified customer data requirement. A transfer above it does not become suspicious by amount alone. The system should record both the threshold decision and the independent risk decision.
-Cross-border interoperability also requires a conflict rule. The ordering VASP may face Pakistan’s minimum fields, a beneficiary jurisdiction’s additional fields, privacy or localisation restrictions and a counterparty protocol’s technical requirements. The final rules should permit additional necessary fields where lawfully required, but require the VASP to identify the legal basis, minimise dat
-FATF revised Recommendation 16 in June 2025 and stated that the changes should apply by the end of 2030. Pakistan’s present rule should therefore be standards-aware but legally time-correct: implement the current VAA and applicable FATF baseline now, design fields and systems that can migrate, and amend the domestic instrument through lawful process when the revised international requirements bec
-The transition should use a published “sunrise” sequence: final rule and schema; provider registration; test environment; bilateral and network conformance; production for high-capability corridors; monitored exception period; full enforcement; and periodic review. Each stage should identify what duty applies, what evidence PVARA will inspect and what happens when a foreign provider cannot receiv
-## 11.9 Self-Hosted Wallets, DeFi and Control Tests
-A transfer involving a self-hosted or unhosted wallet has only one regulated VASP endpoint. It does not have no identifiable actor: the VASP still knows its customer and can collect the intended counterparty, purpose, wallet, asset and transaction information. It also does not automatically have a second VASP capable of receiving a Travel Rule message. Final rules should recognise that difference
-Risk-based controls can include obtaining the counterparty’s name and wallet address, checking sanctions and transaction exposure, asking the customer about purpose and relationship, testing wallet control where proportionate, applying limits or enhanced review, and monitoring the completed transaction. A cryptographic signature, micro-transaction or other proof can show control of a wallet crede
-Restrictions require evidence and a source. A privacy-enhancing asset, mixer exposure, bridge, peer-to-peer transfer or self-hosted wallet may increase opacity or complicate counterparty verification in particular facts. None is inherently proof of laundering. The VASP should record the exposure path, timing, value, service attribution, model confidence, customer explanation and other facts. It m
-“DeFi” similarly describes architecture, not a legal exemption or legal person. FATF’s functional approach asks whether creators, owners, operators or other persons retain control or sufficient influence and perform VASP functions, even where software presents itself as decentralised. The analysis should test:
-| Control surface | Evidence to examine | Regulatory significance |
-|---|---|---|
-| upgrade, pause, mint, seize or parameter keys | key holders, replacement power, multisig quorum and actual use | ability to control core service or customer exposure |
-| front-end and API | operator, geoblocking, fees, order routing and custody connections | performance or facilitation of covered service for users |
-| treasury and fee switch | beneficial recipients, discretionary allocation and revenue dependence | economic control and service business evidence |
-| governance | token concentration, delegation, veto, quorum, off-chain agreements and emergency councils | effective influence, not merely formal voting percentages |
-| oracle, bridge and validator dependencies | selection, replacement, concentration and contractual control | operational control and third-party risk |
-| development and brand | company/foundation role, employment, repositories, marketing and user commitments | relevant context but not alone conclusive |
-The conclusion must identify a person and covered activity. Code cannot file an STR, appoint an MLRO, receive notice or exercise an appeal. If no person performs or controls the regulated service on the evidence, calling the protocol a VASP does not solve supervision. If an identifiable person does, “decentralised” branding does not remove the duty.[^245]
-VASP interaction with DeFi should still be controlled where no DeFi operator is regulated. Product approval should evaluate contract risk, administrator powers, sanctions and illicit-finance exposure, oracle and bridge dependencies, liquidity, transaction finality, customer disclosure, monitoring coverage, custody consequences and incident response. The control is placed on the licensed entity’s
-## 11.10 Investigations, Seizure and Evidentiary Custody
-Financial-integrity systems generate leads and preserve records; they do not confer every investigative power on PVARA, FMU or a VASP. VAA sections 50–61 create offences, investigation and enforcement mechanisms, administrative sanctions, emergency intervention and blocking powers. AMLA gives FMU information and temporary-freeze functions and assigns investigation/prosecution to authorised agenci
-For a digital asset, preservation has two objects: evidence and value. Moving value to a secure wallet may protect it from dissipation but creates a new transaction, fees, tax/accounting questions, key risk and possible contamination of the evidential narrative. Leaving value in place may preserve the original state but allow the controller to move it. An operational protocol should therefore req
-- legal authority, offence or proceeding, issuing actor, time, scope and review route;
-- asset, network, chain identifier, contract, token ID, quantity, address and transaction hash;
-- block height, confirmations, timestamp source, explorer/node and method of acquisition;
-- legal owner, alleged beneficial owner, customer entitlement, custodian and persons with key or account control;
-- key type, device, seed phrase, hardware wallet, multisignature quorum, administrator key and recovery method, without unnecessarily reproducing secrets;
-- valuation source and time, forks, airdrops, staking rewards, rebases, fees and other changes;
-- internal-ledger balances, fiat leg, Travel Rule message, CDD, alerts, STR access restrictions and communications;
-- preservation hash, forensic image, export format, software/version, analyst steps and chain of custody;
-- whether value was frozen, seized, transferred, converted or only observed, and the authority for each act; and
-- protection of unaffected customer assets, return, expenses, forfeiture, disposal and appeal.
-Possession of a key is not possession of an exclusive physical object. A seed can have undisclosed copies; a multisignature wallet requires a quorum; an exchange account may be changed through internal administration without an on-chain signature. Investigators should secure devices, credentials and recovery routes proportionately, change control only where authorised, prevent employees or vendor
-PECA section 31 permits expedited preservation of specified data reasonably required for a criminal investigation where it risks modification, loss, destruction or inaccessibility, subject to written notice and prompt court oversight. Sections 33–35 provide warrant-based search, seizure, access, copying, intelligible output and technical assistance for offences within that Act; section 39 governs
-Cross-border location is normal in virtual-asset cases. A customer may be in Pakistan, the VASP incorporated elsewhere, keys held by a sub-custodian, servers in a third country and value transferable globally. The *Mutual Legal Assistance (Criminal Matters) Act 2020* allows Pakistan to request documents, search, freezing/seizure, tracing and transmission through the central authority; it also per
-The case file must preserve state transitions. An alert becomes a reasoned suspicion; an STR becomes FMU intelligence; intelligence may support an investigation; an investigation may produce admissible evidence; an allegation may result in a finding or acquittal. A sanctions designation can independently trigger a freeze. Recording those transitions protects both effectiveness and fairness and pr
-## 11.11 Effectiveness, Proportionality and Exclusion
-Compliance volume is not effectiveness. Counts of customers rejected, alerts created, STRs filed or transfers blocked can rise because controls are badly tuned. An effective system should measure whether risks were understood, significant cases were detected promptly, reports were useful, assets were lawfully preserved, false positives were corrected, sanctions obligations were met, weak entities
-A balanced performance set should include:
-- completeness and timeliness of CDD and beneficial-ownership refresh;
-- monitoring coverage across on-chain and internal-ledger activity;
-- alert-to-investigation and investigation-to-STR rates by rule, with false-positive and override analysis;
-- STR timeliness, narrative quality, supporting-data completeness and FMU feedback;
-- sanctions-list ingestion latency, potential-match resolution time, confirmed-match action time and erroneous-freeze correction;
-- Travel Rule data completeness, message success, counterparty failures and pending-transfer age;
-- goAML rejection/error rates and entity onboarding status;
-- supervisory findings, repeat breaches, remediation age and outcomes of appeals;
-- de-risking by customer type, geography and product, including unexplained concentration; and
-- enforcement progression from suspicion to investigation, charge, finding, conviction, release and forfeiture, without treating attrition alone as failure.
-Proportionality means controls should increase with demonstrated risk and reduce where risk is lower, while statutory minima remain. FATF’s 2025 revisions emphasised proportionality and financial inclusion. That direction matters in Pakistan, where categorical exclusion of small businesses, overseas Pakistanis, humanitarian activity, rural users or customers associated with a region can push tran
-De-risking must be governed. A VASP may decline or exit a relationship it cannot understand or control, but group labels should not substitute for customer evidence. Decisions should identify the legal or risk basis, senior approval where material, treatment of customer assets, withdrawal or return path, confidentiality limits and complaint or appeal route. AMLA section 7J provides an appeal to t
-Rights also improve detection. A customer who can correct a false name match, outdated beneficial owner or broken Travel Rule message prevents bad data from propagating. A protected analyst who can challenge a vendor score prevents automation bias. An independent sanctions appeal and documented administrative process expose weak rules. Confidentiality remains essential: a right to reasons may be
-Effectiveness review should be periodic and empirical. PVARA, FMU and the National AML/CFT Authority should publish aggregate outcomes without revealing STRs or investigative methods, commission thematic reviews, compare regulatory data with case outcomes, test entity systems and retire rules that create noise without useful intelligence. The question is not whether the framework looks severe. It
-## 11.12 Corrective Financial-Integrity Package
-Pakistan has a primary statutory foundation: the AML bridge, direct VASP and issuer duties, a Travel Rule baseline, reporting interfaces and data limits. Completion requires the following controlled package:
-| Instrument or action | Minimum content | Evidence of completion |
-|---|---|---|
-| AMLA Schedule IV instrument | publish any existing PVARA notification, or notify PVARA under Schedule IV item 1(vi); allocate s 6A supervision, concurrent SBP/SECP work and s 7J appeals | Gazette/SRO text and updated official consolidation |
-| issuer amendment | reporting-entity status, supervisor, CDD/records, FMU channel, sanctions, confidentiality and appeal for every s 46(2) issuer | enacted amendment and commencement |
-| VAA technical correction | replace the anomalous “FMLI” reference with the intended institution; preserve FMU, TFS, investigation and court functions | amending Act[^251] |
-| final PVARA Regulations | MLRO; enterprise/customer risk; CDD/beneficial ownership; monitoring and goAML; cash-only CTR treatment; UN/domestic TFS and CPF; records, privacy, cyber, vendors, inspection, sanctions and transition | final notified text and consultation response[^252] |
-| Travel Rule specification | domestic threshold; **named data schema (IVMS 101 or a named alternative with published mapping)**; fields; valuation, aggregation and structuring; counterparty due diligence; missing data; self-hosted wallets; cross-border conflict; security and retention | machine-readable schema, test cases and commencement |
-| functions protocol | PVARA–FMU–National Authority–SBP–SECP–MOFA–Ministry of Interior/provincial Home Departments–NACTA–investigator hand-offs, each tied to a statute, lawful data set, confidentiality, response time and correction; separate the UN (1948 Act/SRO 261(I)/2019) and domestic ATA designation routes explicitly | signed public protocol with protected operational annex |
-The functions protocol must not create powers. FMU should lead STR/CTR receipt, goAML and intelligence; PVARA should lead VASP preventive supervision after valid AMLA allocation; SBP and SECP should lead their sectoral perimeters with joint-examination rules; the National AML/CFT Authority should lead strategy and performance; competent UN and ATA institutions should lead their separate TFS route
-Technical completion requires entity-level goAML verification, secure credentials, test and production approval, reconciliation between the public licence register and confidential reporting register, and an interoperable Travel Rule conformance suite. Supervision should sample actual onboarding, beneficial ownership, alerts, STR narratives, sanctions matches, Travel Rule failures, model changes,
-Every NOC, sandbox and incumbent file should state authorised activity, conditions, AML supervisor, goAML status, deadline and customer treatment. A draft threshold or private schema is not enforceable law. Completion is proved by the Schedule IV instrument, final Regulations and specification, functions protocol, conformance record and first effectiveness report—not by consultation closure or a
-That last point is no longer hypothetical. The consultation on the VASP Regulations opened on 11 June 2026 and closed on 2 July 2026; at the date of this chapter it has been closed for some seven weeks, PVARA's own instrument register still shows no final Regulations, no threshold has been prescribed under section 47, and no Schedule IV notification has been located. Each of those is individually
-The result is exact. **Deeming creates obligation; designation completes the supervisor. On-chain visibility is not identity. goAML is the reporting channel, not the suspicion test. Travel Rule data must travel securely but need not be written on-chain. AML and TFS may share data, but not a decision rule. A risk signal begins an enquiry; lawful evidence supports an outcome.**
